articles.title: Hypoxia Orchestrates the Natural History of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) arises from a dynamic interplay between epithelial dysfunction, immune activation, microbial dysbiosis and tissue remodelling. Although hypoxia was initially regarded as a consequence of intestinal inflammation, it is now recognized as an active regulator of epithelial, immune and stromal responses that coordinate disease progression. Here, we propose that hypoxia acts as a biological organizer linking oxygen sensing to the transition from intestinal homeostasis to chronic inflammation and structural tissue damage. We use this term in a mechanistic rather than a hierarchical sense: oxygen availability is a shared upstream constraint on epithelial, immune, microbial and stromal programmes, not a single initiating event. This review integrates evidence connecting oxygen sensing with epithelial barrier integrity, immunometabolism, microbial ecology and stromal remodelling, with emphasis on advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial biology and microbiome research. Physiological low-oxygen gradients support epithelial metabolism, barrier integrity and immune tolerance, whereas persistent inflammatory hypoxia drives oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming and maladaptive epithelial-immune-microbial interactions. Hypoxia also contributes to spatially distinct epithelial, immune and stromal niches that may sustain chronic inflammation and fibrotic progression. Microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids and succinate, together with iron metabolism and ferroptosis, further link oxygen sensing to tissue injury, adaptation and repair. These findings position hypoxia-responsive signalling as a pharmacologically actionable network rather than a downstream consequence of inflammation. Targeting selected components may promote mucosal healing and limit structural disease progression, although successful translation will require cell- and isoform-selective modulation, adequate tissue exposure and careful assessment of long-term safety.

articles.title: Antibody-drug conjugates as immune modulators: current landscape, challenges, and opportunities.
articles.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), originally developed for oncology applications, have emerged as a promising targeted therapeutic platform that combines the antigen specificity of monoclonal antibodies with the potency of small-molecule payloads. The clinical success of ADCs in cancer therapy has stimulated a growing interest in its application for immunomodulation, including autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammatory disorders, and transplantation. In the context of immune modulation, ADCs offer the advantage for selective depletion or functional regulation of pathogenic immune cells while maintaining overall immune homeostasis. However, ADC designing for immunological diseases presents unique challenges, including lower antigen expression, distinct immune microenvironments, the need for higher target selectivity prolonged. Furthermore, linker-payload strategies must be carefully tuned to promote immune modulation in pathogenic sites while minimizing off-target effect. This review provides the overall landscape of ADCs for immunomodulatory applications with critical analysis of recent preclinical and clinical advances, highlighting the rationale for target selection and linker-payload design considerations. In addition, we discuss current challenges, lessons learned from oncology ADCs, and future opportunities. We hope this review will be helpful for optimum design of ADC to progress from broad immunosuppression toward a selective immunomodulation in autoimmune diseases, inflammatory disorders, and transplantation.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled nanomedicine development: From rational design to manufacturing optimization.
articles.abstract: The translation of nanomedicines remains constrained by persistent bottlenecks, including complex design parameters, unpredictable in vivo behavior, and low diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI), with its advanced data processing and learning algorithms, offers new solutions to these challenges by learning from heterogeneous data and supporting decision-making throughout nanomedicine development. This review summarizes the AI methods and modeling workflows relevant to nanomedicine and surveys their applications in rational nanomaterial design, prediction of in vivo fate and nano-bio interactions, theranostic imaging analysis, and formulation and manufacturing optimization. This review further discusses the main barriers that currently limit translation, which largely concern data, model reliability, and computational cost. Future progress will depend on better data resources, more generalizable and interpretable models, and closer integration of AI with experimental and mechanistic approaches. We believe that through these advances, AI-enabled nanomedicine will ultimately achieve more reliable and translatable outcomes.

articles.title: From acute intervention to chronic management: Biopharmaceutical barriers and advanced formulation strategies for Peroral metronomic chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: Although cancer is a chronic disease, conventional oncology has largely relied on maximum tolerated dose (MTD) chemotherapy to achieve rapid tumor killing. However, the limited specificity of these agents frequently results in substantial systemic toxicity and necessitates prolonged treatment-free intervals that may permit tumor regrowth and therapeutic resistance. Metronomic chemotherapy (MET) has emerged as a promising alternative approach, characterized by continuous or intermittent administration of low-dose chemotherapeutic agents over extended periods (often incorporating scheduled drug-free breaks ranging from daily up to weekly). Rather than relying primarily on direct cytotoxicity, MET exerts anti-tumor effects through repeated anti-angiogenic activity, immune modulation, and alteration of tumor microenvironment, while minimizing treatment-related toxicity. These properties make MET particularly attractive for long-term cancer management. Despite its clinical promise, broader implementation of MET remains constrained by challenges associated with drug delivery and administration. For chronic therapeutic regimens, the peroral route represents the most practical and patient-friendly option, offering improved adherence, reduced healthcare burden, and fewer hospital visits. However, many chemotherapeutic agents possess poor aqueous solubility, limited membrane permeability, and unfavorable pharmacokinetic properties, resulting in inadequate peroral bioavailability. In this review, we discuss the evolving role of MET in cancer treatment, compare available routes of administration, and examine the major biopharmaceutical barriers to effective peroral delivery. We further highlight emerging formulation strategies and advanced drug delivery systems designed to overcome these limitations. Collectively, these advances may facilitate the transition of cancer therapy from an episodic, high-intensity intervention toward a sustainable long-term disease management strategy.

articles.title: Regulatory landscape for inhaled biologics: Considerations and guidelines.
articles.abstract: Despite significant scientific interest, only a small number of inhaled biologics have reached regulatory approval, reflecting the complex interplay between the inherent structural fragility of biologics during the aerosolization steps intrinsic to inhaled administration and the absence of inhalation-specific regulatory guidance. This review examines the key scientific and technical considerations that influence the stability, safety, and performance of inhaled biologics, including aggregation, chemical degradation, immunogenicity, device compatibility, and the limited availability of inhalation-qualified excipients. Existing regulatory frameworks in the United States and Europe for biological products, inhalation products, and delivery devices provide substantial foundations for inhaled biologic development. Their application requires an integrated assessment of the final formulation-device pairing, particularly where aerosolization alters molecular integrity, biological activity, or pulmonary exposure. This review connects these considerations with clinical experience and proposes a scope for dedicated guidance addressing quality, pulmonary safety, device performance, and clinical benefit. A survey of ongoing clinical trials reveals a growing but constrained pipeline dominated by mRNA therapeutics, protein-based agents, and viral-vectored vaccines, underscoring both progress and persistent formulation barriers. Together, these insights emphasize the urgent need for a harmonized regulatory paradigm tailored to inhaled biologics that integrates biologic-specific analytical expectations, aerosolization stress testing, and clear pathways for excipient qualification.

articles.title: Drug resistance mechanisms and sensitization strategies in central nervous system tumors.
articles.abstract: Central nervous system tumors remain challenging owing to their location, heterogeneity, and relapse, with persistently high mortality to incidence ratios. Current standard therapy (surgery plus temozolomide based chemoradiotherapy) remains first line, yet nearly all patients eventually develop acquired resistance, the major hurdle to survival benefit. Resistance is not driven by single gene mutations but by a multidimensional adaptive network from nucleus to intercellular communication. In the nucleus, backup DNA repair pathways activate with epigenetic regulation, allowing cells to escape via lineage reprogramming or senescence. In the cytoplasm, metabolic reprogramming affects epigenetic enzymes and reshapes antioxidant/repair networks. At the membrane, the blood brain and blood tumor barriers not only physically block drugs but also actively remodel to promote resistance. In intercellular communication, immunosuppressive cells (Tregs, M2 macrophages) and neuron glioma synapses provide signals and metabolic support. Emerging sensitizing strategies include targeting repair, blocking plasticity, eliminating senescent cells, computational combination therapy, epigenetic metabolic interventions, biomimetic delivery, immune microenvironment remodeling, and disrupting neuro tumor crosstalk-but are limited by BBB penetration, preclinical model fidelity, and target selectivity. This review organizes current evidence by spatial mechanisms and proposes a multi modal personalized sensitization framework centered on overcoming barriers, aiming to provide a theoretical reference for precision therapy.

articles.title: Advances in Attribution and Management of NPSLE Manifestations of Lupus: Current Paradigms and Emerging Evidence.
articles.abstract: Neuropsychiatric involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus remains a significant clinical challenge, encompassing a broad spectrum of manifestations affecting both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Accurate diagnosis and attribution require a structured approach, ideally supported by a multidisciplinary team evaluation and the application of validated attribution models. Recent evidence has reinforced the utility of existing algorithms in improving the attribution of neuropsychiatric events to systemic lupus erythematosus, with advances in laboratory testing and neuroimaging enhancing the ability to establish a causal link between the disease and its clinical manifestations. In parallel, emerging insights into disease pathogenesis are helping to clarify the role of targeted therapeutic strategies, closely tied to attribution processes. High-dose glucocorticoids plus cyclophosphamide remain the cornerstone for severe, inflammatory, neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus, while rituximab has shown the most consistent signal in refractory disease, albeit mainly in uncontrolled studies. Therapeutic development is progressively expanding along the B-cell lineage, from enhanced CD20 targeting (e.g., obinutuzumab) to profound B-cell depletion via chimeric antigen-T-cell-based strategies, and further toward upstream and parallel pathway modulation, including dual BAFF/APRIL blockade with telitacicept and type I interferon receptor inhibition with anifrolumab, both currently supported by case-based evidence. This narrative review summarizes recent developments in the diagnosis, attribution, pathogenesis, and treatment of neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus, with the aim of providing clinicians with an updated framework to better recognize and manage this complex and often underappreciated manifestation, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: I Have a Medical Degree. Should I Consider a Career in Clinical Pharmacology in 2026?
Pharmacological targeting of phosphodiesterase-5 halts pulmonary fibrosis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition via cGMP/PKG/Smad/HDAC2 pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive and incurable disease with activation of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) as a crucial pathological step. Despite advances in elucidating its pathogenesis, therapeutic options for PF remain very limited. Although raising intracellular levels of cGMP mitigated fibrosis in animal models, the mechanism(s) underlying this action, particularly concerning EMT, remain unclear. PDE5, a key cGMP-hydrolyzing enzyme, is a promising therapeutic target, as some PDE5 inhibitors are in clinical use. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Two well-established rat models of PF, induced by bleomycin or paraquat were used to elucidate the therapeutic potential and mechanisms underpinning effects of the PDE5 inhibitor tadalafil on pulmonary fibrogenesis. KEY RESULTS: Daily administration of tadalafil attenuated PF development and lung injury. even when administered at an advanced stage of PF, tadalafil significantly attenuated fibrotic progression and improved lung histopathology. Mechanistically, tadalafil exerted its therapeutic effect by suppressing the canonical TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway and EMT through a cGMP/PKG pathway. Immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence analyses corroborated the in‑vivo antifibrotic activity of tadalafil. Preliminary results indicated PKG‑dependent down-regulation of histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) expression and elevated acetylated histones. Knockdown and pharmacological inhibition of HDAC2 mimicked effects of tadalafil, whereas over-expression of HDAC2 negated tadalafil's effects on EMT, implying a key mechanistic role for HDAC2. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Tadalafil halted progression of PF by inhibiting EMT, most likely through a PKG-mediated pathway counteracting TGF-β-induced HDAC2 expression. Our findings, together with the well-tolerated safety profile. warrant immediate clinical assessment of repurposing tadalafil for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and nontraditional health outcomes: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: AIM: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are prescribed for cardiovascular and renal protection, but their effects on nontraditional health outcomes remain unclear. With the increasing use of ARBs in diverse populations, clarifying their broader impact has important clinical implications. METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed ARBs and nontraditional health outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Where trial-level data were available, we re-analysed outcomes using random-effects models and evaluated heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, and small-study effects. RESULTS: Fifteen systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs were included, covering 35 unique nontraditional outcomes. Nine outcomes reached nominal statistical significance, but only a few met more stringent credibility criteria. The most credible associations were lower risks of headache and new-onset diabetes, and lower fasting plasma insulin levels with ARB therapy. Associations with migraine severity, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and insulin resistance were suggestive or exploratory because of prediction intervals crossing the null, sparse data, heterogeneity, or limited certainty. No convincing evidence supported associations with oncological, infectious, or transplant-related outcomes. Most included reviews were rated as low or critically low-quality using AMSTAR 2, warranting cautious interpretation. CONCLUSION: ARBs appear to provide therapeutic benefits beyond traditional indications, particularly in metabolic and neurological domains, without evidence of excess harm. These findings may inform clinical decision-making in patients at risk of diabetes or with comorbid pain conditions.

articles.title: Degraders take on GPCRs.
RDP-modified extracellular vesicles from brain organoid-derived mesenchymal stem cells improve the behavior and pathology of 5×FAD mice.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which treatment options remain limited. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer a potential cell-free therapeutic approach, but limited brain exposure after systemic administration remains a major obstacle. Mesenchymal stem-like cells derived from human brain organoids (hBO-MSCs) may provide an alternative EV source with a molecular profile shaped by the neural culture environment. This study aimed to generate RDP-modified hBO-MSC-EVs and evaluate their physicochemical characteristics, acute safety, brain-associated biodistribution, and treatment-associated effects in the 5×FAD mouse model of AD. hBO-MSCs were isolated from dorsal forebrain-like human brain organoids and engineered to express an RDP-Lamp2b-HA fusion protein. EV preparations were characterized by morphology, particle measurements, EV-associated protein markers, and relative RDP-Lamp2b-HA abundance. Brain-associated biodistribution and acute safety were assessed in C57BL/6J mice, whereas treatment-associated outcomes were evaluated in 5×FAD mice receiving PBS, unmodified hBO-MSC-EVs, or hBO-MSC-RDP-EVs. Behavioral testing, hippocampal Aβ histopathology, and exploratory transcriptomic profiling were used to assess the response. Following intravenous administration, RDP modification was associated with greater brain-associated fluorescence than unmodified EVs, without evidence of overt acute organ histopathology or a consistent systemic pro-inflammatory response at the tested endpoints. In 5×FAD mice, hBO-MSC-RDP-EV treatment was associated with improvements in selected behavioral measures, most consistently in the Morris water maze, together with reduced histologically detectable hippocampal Aβ plaque burden and changes in inflammation- and neuronal-associated transcripts. These findings warrant further preclinical evaluation of surface-engineered hBO-MSC-EVs as a candidate cell-free approach for AD. Intact-EV blood-brain barrier transport, cargo-dependent mechanisms, source-specific advantages, and long-term safety remain unestablished.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomics positively impacts polypharmacy-related toxicity and clinical outcomes in psychiatric patients.
articles.abstract: Polypharmacy is the concurrent use of five or more medications and often leads to serious Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs), mostly affecting elderly patients. Polypharmacy, which impacts up to 40% of elderly European patients, can not only increase the occurrence of ADRs, hospitalization days, and readmissions but is also reciprocally associated with increased healthcare costs and poor quality of life of the patients. Here, we performed a detailed analysis of the impact of polypharmacy on increased drug toxicity, hospitalization days, higher incidence of hospital readmission, healthcare utilization, and patients' quality of life between the PGx-guided and control study arms of our large PREPARE psychiatric cohort. Our data show that patients in the PGx-guided arm exhibited significantly lower rates of both combined (41.95%) and psychiatric polypharmacy (20.7%) compared to those in the control arm (49.8% and 26.1%, respectively). Also, polypharmacy patients from the PGx-guided arm received fewer co-medications than those in the control arm, suggesting that genome-guided drug dose optimization can reduce the risks associated with complex regimens. Interestingly, patients in the PGx-guided arm had about half the risk of hospitalization in the presence of psychiatric polypharmacy (RR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.36-0.67, p<0.001). These data indicate that PGx-guided prescribing changes the selection and dosing of drugs rather than their number. Our findings underline that incorporation of PGx testing in psychiatric patients' drug management will allow physicians to refine treatment options towards optimized, targeted therapies, which will not only reduce the occurrence of ADRs and disease complications but can also decrease the overall financial burden of healthcare services.

articles.title: A Hsp70-dependent bioorthogonal platform for tumor-specific drug release.
articles.abstract: Here, we present a novel Hsp70-dependent bioorthogonal prodrug platform that integrates tumor-selective accumulation with inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) chemistry to enable spatiotemporally controlled drug release. We constructed a tetrazine (Tz)-functionalized Hsp70 inhibitor Tz-S1g, along with trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrugs TCO-DOX and TCO-MZ1. Tz-S1g selectively accumulates in tumor cells via high-affinity binding to overexpressed and activated Hsp70, which is characteristic of malignant cells. In tumor microenvironments, Tz-S1g rapidly triggers the IEDDA reaction to liberate active DOX and MZ1, and fully restores cytotoxicity, and BRD4 degradation in tumor cells, whereas minimal activation and cytotoxicity occur in normal cells. In vivo studies have shown that this strategy can effectively inhibit tumor growth in both B16 tumor-bearing mice and MDA-MB-231 tumor-bearing mice, while avoiding systemic toxicity. This Hsp70 bioorthogonal strategy offers a general, safe, and efficient platform for the tumor-specific activation of chemotherapeutic agents and PROTACs, significantly improving therapeutic selectivity and safety.

articles.title: Masitinib-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticles reinstate lysosomal acidification and drive immunomodulation in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) poses a formidable therapeutic challenge due to its intricate pathological mechanisms and the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Via transcriptomic analyses and experimental validation, we identify that a malignant neuro-immune pathological cycle, driven by neuronal lysosomal acidification dysfunction and microglial immune activation, potently accelerates AD pathogenesis. Then, we engineer a simple bifunctional intranasal delivery system (PLGA@M) by loading masitinib into poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles. Following intranasal administration, PLGA@M bypasses the BBB to enter the brain directly via olfactory and trigeminal nerves. PLGA degrades to release acidic moieties, lowering lysosomal pH and restoring autophagic flux, while masitinib inhibits microglial colony stimulating factor 1 receptor signaling, attenuating microglial proliferation, excessive activation and neuroinflammation. Behavioral assays confirm that PLGA@M markedly reverses cognitive deficits in AD mice. This system upgrades PLGA from a mere carrier to a therapeutic component, featuring simplicity, high efficiency and great clinical translation potential.

articles.title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment.
articles.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LACNE. Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LACNE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LACNE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LACNE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

articles.title: Fatty acid-derived dicarboxylic acid modification mitigates human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate-induced interstitial lung disease.
articles.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has transformed human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted cancer therapy, but its clinical use is constrained by interstitial lung disease (ILD), a potentially fatal toxicity linked to pulmonary macrophage handling of circulating antibody-drug conjugates. Here, we develop fatty acid-derived dicarboxylic acid modification as a host-facing antibody engineering strategy to reduce alveolar macrophage-associated pulmonary uptake while preserving HER2-directed tumor specificity. Using N-hydroxysuccinimide ester chemistry, we coupled mono-N-hydroxysuccinimide-activated esters of C4, C12, and C18 aliphatic dicarboxylic acids to surface-accessible amino groups on trastuzumab, generating C4-DA-, C12-DA-, and C18-DA-modified conjugates with a retained distal carboxyl group and an average of approximately four added groups per antibody. Dicarboxylic acid modification preserved HER2 binding but reduced Fcγ receptor engagement in a chain-length-dependent manner, with C18-DA modification abolishing detectable FcγRIII binding under the tested conditions. This receptor-level shift reduced macrophage-associated antibody uptake by up to approximately 42% across mouse alveolar macrophages, mouse macrophages, and human macrophage-like cells, while maintaining HER2-positive tumor-cell binding and endocytic trafficking. In vivo, dicarboxylic acid-modified trastuzumab reduced pulmonary deposition without compromising tumor localization. C18-DA-modified trastuzumab showed greater mouse serum albumin binding, and the corresponding antibody-drug conjugate exhibited increased systemic exposure and reduced clearance. In a repeated-dose immunocompetent model, C12-DA- and C18-DA-modified T-DXd reduced lung weight, selected inflammatory cytokine responses, and pneumonia/ILD-like lesion incidence, with C18-DA modification lowering lesion incidence from 100% to 41.7%. Importantly, dicarboxylic acid-modified T-DXd retained HER2-dependent cytotoxicity and antitumor efficacy in HER2-positive models. Together, our study expands antibody-drug conjugate design beyond tumor targeting and payload optimization, showing that engineering host-cell recognition can improve safety while preserving antitumor function.

articles.title: An injectable dynamic double-network hydrogel induces synergistic tumor pyroptosis and immune activation for potent anti-cancer immunity.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to the limited efficacy of conventional systemic therapies. Herein, we report an injectable dynamic double-network hydrogel Gel@R/N, composed of poly(vinyl alcohol) and tannic acid crosslinked via dynamic boronate ester bonds, for the localized co-delivery of an immune adjuvant (R848) and a pyroptosis inducer (Nigericin) to achieve synergistic tumor ablation and immune activation. The self-healing capacity and pH-responsive drug release properties of this hydrogel enables precise intratumoral administration and sustained release within the acidic tumor microenvironment. Mechanistically, nigericin induces mitochondrial dysfunction and reactive oxygen species accumulation, thus activating the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway to trigger pyroptosis with a cell death rate of 26.4% alongside immunogenic cell death. The release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) caused by pyroptosis, further promoted dendritic cell maturation to 20.8% and macrophage repolarization toward the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype reaching 23.0%. Concurrently, R848 activates Toll-like receptor signaling to promote dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. Additionally, the hydrogel system effectively suppressed tumor growth in both subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma models, accompanied by a 1.55-fold increase in intratumoral CD8+ T cells infiltration and a 65.9% reduction in immunosuppressive cell populations. Overall, this work presents a safe and effective hydrogel-based platform for synergistic pyroptosis induction and immune activation, which offers a promising strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma immunity.

articles.title: Membrane retention and cellular uptake of click conjugated cargos.
articles.abstract: Metabolic glycan labeling offers a facile yet powerful method to functionalize cell membranes with clickable chemical tags for subsequent conjugation of cargos via bioorthogonal click chemistries. However, the membrane retention and cellular uptake of covalently conjugated cargos, which is distinct from natural systems where cells interact with extracellular cargos via electrostatic or hydrophobic interactions, remain elusive. Here, we developed a dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO)-functionalized polyacrylic acid (PAA) probe system that enables simultaneous detection of overall cellular uptake and membrane retention, and investigated how the molecular weight, valency, and hydrophobicity of DBCO-PAAs impact their membrane retention and cell uptake rates after click conjugation to azido-labeled cells. PAA with lower molecular weights exhibited enhanced cell-conjugation efficiency and prolonged membrane retention compared to higher molecular-weight counterparts. Increasing DBCO density improved the cell-conjugation efficiency and membrane retention, while altering the hydrophobicity of PAA induced minimal changes in the membrane retention and cellular internalization rates. We further uncovered energy dependent endocytosis and caveolin-dependent pathways as the main endocytic routes for the covalently conjugated cargos. We also studied the membrane retention of DBCO-functionalized phycoerythrin and allophycocyanin, two representative fluorescent proteins, on azido-labeled cells, which exhibited cargo and cell type-dependent membrane retention. Our study comprehensively assesses the membrane retention and cellular uptake of covalently conjugated cargos and could guide future design of cell-targeting clickable agents.

articles.title: 20(S)-protopanaxatriol inhibits inflammasome activation and ameliorates inflammasome-mediated inflammation in mouse models.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome (NLRP3) is a cytoplasmic complex that drives many inflammatory diseases. However, no NLRP3-targeting therapies have reached clinical approval. PURPOSE: 20(S)-protopanaxatriol (PPT), the aglycone and final metabolite of PPT-type ginsenosides with known anti-inflammatory activity, has been widely studied, yet its mode of action remains insufficiently defined. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms through which PPT regulated NLRP3 inflammasome activation and mediated anti-inflammatory effects in mice. METHODS: We employed limited proteolysis-mass spectrometry to identify NLRP3 as a direct target of PPT, and validated this interaction using cellular thermal shift assay, site-directed mutagenesis, co-immunoprecipitation, and surface plasmon resonance. The effect of PPT on NLRP3 inflammasome activation was assessed in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-primed and nigericin-activated iBMDMs. Furthermore, the in vivo efficacy of PPT was evaluated in two mouse models: LPS-induced acute lung injury (ALI) and monosodium urate-induced peritonitis. RESULTS: PPT interacted with NLRP3 and reduced the NLRP3-NEK7 association. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations analyses predicted that Arg235 and Arg260 may contribute to the modeled binding pocket, which in turn prevented inflammasome assembly and suppressed caspase-1 activation and cleavage of interleukin-1β. Furthermore, PPT markedly reduced inflammatory responses in vitro and ameliorated NLRP3 inflammasome-driven pathology in mouse models. Notably, PPT failed to exert protective effects in the LPS induced ALI model in NLRP3⁻/⁻ mice. CONCLUSION: Taken together, these findings identified PPT as a potential natural compound for the prevention or treatment of NLRP3-driven inflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Tangeretin alleviates airway hyperresponsiveness through epithelial prostaglandin E2 signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) is driven by airway inflammation together with disrupted epithelial-smooth muscle signaling. Current therapies mainly target inflammation or directly relax airway smooth muscle (ASM), whereas strategies aimed at restoring endogenous epithelial control of ASM tone remain incompletely explored. Using target prediction and screening, we identified tangeretin as a candidate modulator of airway epithelial cells (AECs) that may regulate neighboring ASM function. PURPOSE: To determine whether tangeretin modulates epithelial-smooth muscle crosstalk, elucidate the underlying mechanism and evaluate its therapeutic effect in AHR. STUDY DESIGN: Ex vivo functional assays, primary cell experiments and a murine asthma model were combined for investigation. METHODS: A network pharmacology approach was used to predict candidate targets, which were then evaluated by pharmacological validation and molecular docking. Contractile tension recordings were performed in isolated mouse tracheal rings with intact or denuded epithelium. Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) release from primary mouse AECs was quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Whole-cell currents were recorded by patch clamp technique. ASM membrane potential was assessed using DiBAC4(3)-based fluorescence imaging. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma model was established to evaluate the effects of nebulized tangeretin on AHR and lung function. AHR was assessed by whole-body plethysmography as methacholine-induced enhanced pause (Penh) and lung function was evaluated by forced expiratory manoeuvres. RESULTS: Tangeretin induced concentration-dependent relaxation of mouse tracheal rings in an epithelium-dependent manner. Cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition attenuated tangeretin-evoked relaxation. Molecular docking suggested relatively modest predicted non-covalent interactions between tangeretin and COX-1/2, consistent with increased PGE2 release from primary AECs. Antagonism of E-type prostanoid receptor 2 (EP2) or EP4 receptors, or inhibition of the large conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channel (BKCa), significantly reduced tangeretin-induced relaxation. Patch clamp recordings further verified that PGE2 markedly enhanced outward currents in ASM cells, which were inhibited by the selective BKCa blocker iberiotoxin. Supernatant from tangeretin-treated AECs triggered ASM membrane hyperpolarization, while L-type voltage-dependent Ca2+ channel (VDCC) blockade attenuated the relaxation elicited by tangeretin. Tangeretin also retained partial relaxant activity under high-K+ depolarizing conditions. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, nebulized tangeretin reduced methacholine-induced increases in the Penh index and improved FEV100/FVC, with effects similar to salbutamol. However, COX inhibition diminished the bronchodilatory effects of tangeretin. Moreover, nebulized tangeretin ameliorated OVA-induced type 2 inflammation. CONCLUSION: Tangeretin may promote COX-dependent PGE2 production in AECs, which engages an EP receptor-BKCa-VDCC suppression cascade to reduce ASM contractility and AHR. These findings identify an epithelium-driven mechanism underlying tangeretin-induced ASM relaxation and provide a rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in asthma.

articles.title: The H2S-releasing metformin hybrid Met-ITC protects against diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction preserving glycaemic control.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Patients undergoing metformin (Met) therapy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes remain at high cardiovascular risk. Hydrogen sulphide (H2S)-releasing molecules offer antioxidant, anti-senescence and vasoactive properties that may complement Met activity. This study investigated whether metformin-isothiocyanate (Met-ITC), a H2S-releasing metformin hybrid, preserves the antidiabetic activity of Met while providing H2S-derived vascular protection. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: The predicted Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) properties of Met and Met-ITC were evaluated in silico. Maintenance of Met antidiabetic properties was assessed in vitro by evaluating glucose uptake in HepG2 cells and in vivo through oral glucose tolerance tests in db/db mice. The ability of Met-ITC to release H2S and its ability to preserve cell viability and contrast ROS formation and cellular senescence were evaluated in human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) exposed to hydrogen peroxide, homocysteine or high-glucose concentrations. The hyperpolarizing effect of Met-ITC was tested on HASMCs and its direct vasorelaxing effect as well as its ability to inhibit noradrenaline-induced vasoconstriction were tested on endothelium-intact or -denuded rat aortic rings. KEY RESULTS: Met-ITC showed a more favourable permeability profile than Met and maintained its antidiabetic profile. It provided better protection against oxidative stress, loss of cell viability and senescence compared with Met. Moreover, Met-ITC produced a concentration-dependent hyperpolarization of HASMCs, restricted noradrenaline-induced contraction and induced vasodilatation in endothelium-denuded and -intact rat aortic rings. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: These findings identify Met-ITC as a potential candidate for the treatment of diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction.

articles.title: The efficacy of taurolidine lock solution in preventing catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatrics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of taurolidine lock solutions in preventing catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatric patients with central venous access devices. METHODS: This meta-analysis systematically searched four electronic databases to identify studies comparing taurolidine with standard lock solutions for catheter lock in pediatric patients. The primary outcome measure was the incidence density of catheter-related bloodstream infections. Secondary outcomes included the incidence density of central line-associated bloodstream infection, cumulative incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections, catheter removal due to infection, central venous access device (CVAD)-related thrombosis, and adverse events. Random-effects models were used to pool incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for incidence-density outcomes and risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes, with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: In the primary analysis of five studies, taurolidine-containing catheter lock solutions were associated with a significantly lower incidence rate of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) compared with control solutions (IRR = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.15-0.36; I2 = 0%; P < 0.00001). The separate secondary analysis of three studies also showed a lower incidence density of central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (IRR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.08-0.85; I2 = 90%; P = 0.03). The cumulative incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections was lower in the taurolidine group (RR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.23-0.61; I2 = 54%; P = 0.0001). No statistically significant differences were detected in catheter removal due to infection (RR = 1.25, 95% CI: 0.60-2.62; I2 = 12%; P = 0.56), CVAD-related thrombosis (RR = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.29-2.64; I2 = 0%; P = 0.82), or adverse events (RR = 3.93, 95% CI: 0.82-18.80; I2 = 64%; P = 0.09). CONCLUSION: Taurolidine-containing lock solutions may reduce the incidence density and cumulative incidence of CRBSI in pediatric patients requiring central venous access. However, the available evidence is insufficient to establish their comparative safety. Given the substantial heterogeneity, mixed study designs, variability in infection definitions, and limited safety data, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Further large-scale, multicenter randomized controlled trials with adequate safety monitoring are needed before broad routine implementation can be recommended. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251162414 identifier, CRD420251162414.

articles.title: The efficacy and safety of combining different commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations with conventional Western drugs in the treatment of diabetic osteoporosis: a network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biomedicine for diabetic osteoporosis (DOP) is often associated with serious side effects, such as osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures. In contrast, recent clinical studies have highlighted the potential of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations (CCPPs) as effective alternatives. These studies suggest that CCPPs help increase bone mineral density, relieve pain, regulate bone turnover markers, and lower blood glucose, thereby improving osteoporosis. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of six CCPPs combined with biomedicine for the treatment of DOP. A network meta-analysis (NMA) was used to compare and rank the therapeutic effects of these CCPPs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive search of multiple databases up to November 2025 to screen for studies assessing the effectiveness of CCPPs for DOP. Two independent reviewers performed study screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool version 2.0, and the certainty of evidence was graded according to the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework. Continuous outcomes were expressed as mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); dichotomous outcomes were summarized as odds ratios (OR) or risk ratios (RR) with their corresponding 95% CIs. All analyses were completed using StataMP 18 software, and treatment rankings were determined using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) method. RESULTS: This study included 34 studies involving 3,720 patients with DOP, evaluating six different CCPP regimens. All CCPP regimens showed benefits in increasing bone mineral density, relieving pain, regulating bone turnover markers, and lowering blood glucose. Compared with biomedicine alone, CCPPs combined with biomedicine demonstrated superior outcomes in overall response rate, bone mineral density, bone turnover markers, alkaline phosphatase reduction, and fasting blood glucose, while also showing a lower incidence of adverse events. Specifically, the Guskang (GSK) regimen ranked highest in overall response rate; Xianling Gubao (XLGB), Jintiange (JTG), and GSK showed notable effects on improving bone mineral density; JTG was best for increasing osteocalcin levels; XLGB ranked highest for calcium and phosphorus; and Liuwei Dihuang Wan (LWDHW) produced the greatest reduction in fasting blood glucose. GL had the lowest incidence of adverse events. CONCLUSION: Compared with biomedicine alone, combining CCPPs with biomedicine for DOP treatment improves clinical outcomes. However, high-quality, rigorously designed clinical trials are needed to validate these preliminary results. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251240840, identifier CRD420251240840.

articles.title: Acknowledgement to Referees.
Linking kinase inhibitors for greater selectivity.
Checkpoint inhibitor combinations: the trial-to-approval gap.
Comparing the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin e with vitamin e alone on mastodynia due to fibrocystic breast disease: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mastodynia is a common symptom in women with fibrocystic breast disease and can substantially impair quality of life. Although vitamin E is frequently used for symptom relief, the potential additional analgesic effect of fluoxetine remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin E with that of vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease. METHODS: This double-blind, randomized clinical trial enrolled 78 women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease who attended clinics affiliated with Shahrekord University of Medical Sciences, Shahrekord, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus fluoxetine (10 mg/day) or vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus placebo for 8 weeks. Randomization was computer-generated, allocation was concealed using identical medication packaging, and participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was breast pain intensity, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline and at 1 and 2 months after treatment initiation. Secondary outcomes included breast heaviness, breast itching, and adverse events. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and appropriate categorical tests. Seventy participants (35 per group) completed the study and were included in the analysis. RESULTS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Repeated-measures analysis of variance demonstrated significant effects of treatment group (F (1,68) = 11.056, P = 0.001), time (F (2,136) = 164.321, P < 0.001), and the group-by-time interaction (F (2,136) = 60.996, P < 0.001) on breast pain intensity. No significant between-group differences were observed at baseline or after 1 month of treatment; however, after 2 months, breast pain intensity was significantly lower in the fluoxetine plus vitamin E group than in the vitamin E plus placebo group (P < 0.001). Breast heaviness was also significantly less frequent in the combination therapy group after 1 month (P = 0.009). Three participants in the fluoxetine group discontinued treatment because of adverse events, and no serious adverse events were reported in either group. CONCLUSIONS: The addition of fluoxetine to vitamin E improved breast pain after 8 weeks compared with vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease. These findings suggest that fluoxetine may be a useful adjunctive treatment; however, larger multicenter randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20200205046381N1), registered on February 28, 2020.

articles.title: MYC in renal cell carcinoma pathogenic mechanisms and pharmacological intervention strategies.
articles.abstract: As a pleiotropic master transcriptional regulator that controls an extensive, context-dependent repertoire of target genes governing cell-fate determination, the oncoprotein c-Myc has long been regarded as an "undruggable" therapeutic target. In renal cell carcinoma (RCC), aberrant c‑Myc activation serves as a critical driver of tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, rendering it a high‑priority yet therapeutically intractable target for pharmacological intervention. To systematically delineate the research landscape and translational potential of c‑Myc in RCC, this review summarizes current advances from multiple dimensions. The structural features and physiological functions of c-Myc are first introduced, after which the role of dysregulated c-Myc signaling in mediating key malignant phenotypes of RCC, including excessive proliferation, metastasis, immune escape, and therapeutic resistance, is comprehensively summarized. Subsequently, mainstream pharmacological strategies targeting MYC signaling are reviewed, with emphasis on their molecular mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, and prospects for clinical translation. Furthermore, natural bioactive compounds and traditional Chinese medicine formulas with the potential to modulate MYC signaling in RCC are systematically categorized, with emphasis on their regulatory mechanisms, including MYC transcriptional inhibition, c-Myc protein destabilization, remodeling of downstream oncogenic transcriptional networks, and translational potential. This review integrates updated pathogenic mechanisms and pharmacological advances, providing a concise theoretical basis for developing c‑Myc-targeted innovative drugs against RCC.

articles.title: Future directions and challenges of drug development and non-human primate models.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Gene and cell therapy are transforming therapeutic approaches for genetic diseases and malignancies. This review examines the current role and future directions of non-human primate (NHP) models in preclinical safety evaluation of adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy amid accelerating adoption of new approach methodologies (NAMs). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure for publications from January 2015 to June 2026; approximately 60 English-language and 5 Chinese-language publications, together with FDA, EMA, and NMPA guidance documents, were included. KEY FINDINGS: NHPs remain the reference species for AAV and CAR-T safety evaluation, yet supply crises, ethical pressures, and documented prediction gaps (hepatotoxicity, dorsal root ganglion injury) are driving NAMs adoption. Organoids, organs-on-chips (87% sensitivity and 100% specificity for drug-induced liver injury), and AI-driven models are maturing under the FDA Modernization Act 2.0 and the 2025 FDA roadmap. SIGNIFICANCE: We propose the Hierarchical Replacement Assessment Framework (HRAF), a three-tier, two-threshold model that reallocates NHP resources from routine screening to risk confirmation, providing an actionable roadmap for mechanism-based and welfare-conscious preclinical development.

articles.title: Optimizing the molar ratio in co-amorphous systems: Molecular mechanisms, screening methods, and critical quality attributes.
articles.abstract: Co-amorphous systems (CAMS) are promising for formulating poorly water-soluble drugs and enhancing their oral bioavailability, without the high mass-fraction burdens and hygroscopic instability associated with traditional polymer-based amorphous solid dispersions. Recent progress notwithstanding, the selection of component stoichiometry remains an empirical bottleneck as formulation workflows have traditionally assumed a 1:1 equimolar ratio. A 1:1 default can be associated with excess localized free volume and uncomplexed polyfunctional binding sites that promote homonucleation and phase separation. This review evaluates the molecular, thermodynamic, and physical mechanisms dictating optimal co-amorphous molar ratios. We discuss glass transition-based screening as a quick first filter, and the orthogonal and confirmatory tests (spectroscopic, solid-state NMR, dielectric, stability studies) needed to select a formulation, including a proposed strategy for cases where the optimal ratios for stability and dissolution differ. Crucially, the optimal ratio is conditional and can shift with humidity and preparation route. A systematic analysis of recent literature (2021-2026) demonstrates that while 67.7% of dedicated optimization studies identified non-equimolar optimal compositions, only 11.3% of publications systematically screen composition. Finally, we outline emerging in silico approaches that may reduce the experimental effort of ratio screening.

articles.title: Myelin in a dish? Proving it's myelin.
Multi-target effects and clinical optimization treatment strategies of recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide in acute heart failure and myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Acute cardiovascular diseases have become a serious public health challenge worldwide. Optimizing treatment strategies is crucial for improving the prognosis of patients. Recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide (rhBNP) has garnered significant attention due to its multi-target mechanisms of action. This article aims to comprehensively review the multi-target effects of rhBNP in the treatment of acute cardiovascular diseases, and briefly explain its molecular mechanism through the activation of natriuretic peptide receptors and multiple downstream signaling pathways. In addition, combined with the latest clinical evidence, the optimization strategies for the clinical application of rhBNP are deeply discussed. However, it is important to acknowledge that current clinical evidence regarding renal protection and long-term clinical outcomes remains mixed. This review aims to provide evidence-based, individualized treatment recommendations for clinical practice, thereby improving the clinical outcomes of patients with acute cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Supramolecular soft matter in traditional Chinese medicine: multiscale structure-function evidence, critical limitations, and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Plant metabolites used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can form supramolecular assemblies in decoctions or in formulations prepared from purified molecules. These experimental settings support different conclusions. This narrative review examines TCM-derived supramolecular soft matter (TCM-derived SSM) through relationships among molecular interactions, assembly structure, physicochemical properties, and biological responses. It distinguishes assemblies isolated from decoctions, recombined extracts, formulations prepared from purified metabolites, and mixtures of defined metabolites with extracts. Micelles, vesicles, nanoparticles (NPs), nanofibers (NFs), and supramolecular gels provide examples, while carbonized products and covalently crosslinked carriers are discussed as related materials with distinct formation mechanisms. Selected studies associate morphology, surface chemistry, or deformability with altered delivery and preclinical activity. However, the presence of particles, successful reconstitution, and improved efficacy do not individually establish that an assembly is necessary for the effect of a complete preparation. Our contribution is an evidence-oriented comparison of preparation routes, structural measurements, biological comparisons, and the limits of inference across these preparations. We also examine artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted modeling and candidate critical quality attributes (CQAs) within a Quality by Design (QbD) perspective. Predictive design and assembly-based quality control are presented as research prospects that require reproducible measurements, appropriate controls, and validation across batches and biological settings. Self-assembly is a general physicochemical phenomenon; TCM provides a context for studying defined botanical drug combinations and preparation processes rather than evidence of properties unique to one medical tradition. We position this physical-state perspective within the established literature on synergy, antagonism and pharmacokinetic interactions in botanical mixtures.

articles.title: Tryptophan metabolism circadian regulation: clinical and pharmacological implications.
articles.abstract: Circadian clocks are endogenous systems that synchronize physiology and behavior to the light-dark cycle, regulating sleep-wake timing, hormonal rhythms, metabolism and immunity. Among metabolic pathways tightly linked to circadian rhythm, tryptophan (Trp) metabolism occupies a central position because its catabolism through the kynurenine (Kyn) pathway, the serotonin (5-HT)-melatonin pathway and the microbiota-derived indole-AhR pathway, produce molecules endowed with significant neuro-modulatory and immunoregulatory activities and directly involved in circadian regulation. Emerging evidence supports a bidirectional relationship between the clock system and Trp metabolism. The molecular clock regulates expression and activity of key Trp enzymes, creating time-of-day variation in Trp flux, Kyn-Trp ratio, serotonin/melatonin synthesis and AhR ligands availability. Conversely, Trp-derived metabolites in turn modulate clock function and downstream physiology, such as diurnal variations in metabolism and immune response. Here we discuss recent studies highlighting how this interplay has important pathophysiological implications and disruption of Trp metabolism oscillatory pattern influences our susceptibility to developing diseases, such as infectious, metabolic and neuropsychiatric diseases. Moreover, we highlight the importance of considering daily fluctuation when using these molecules as biomarkers and interpreting them in a clinical setting. Among circadian-based interventions, such as chronotherapy, light therapy or time-restricted feeding, we propose pharmacological targeting of Trp pathways or pharmacological use of Trp derivatives as a novel approach of circadian medicine, able to improve clinical outcomes across various fields.

articles.title: Traditional medicinal plants in the Unified Health System of Brazil: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: The Brazilian National List of Medicinal Plants of Interest to the Unified Health System (RENISUS) was created to guide the incorporation of botanical drugs into public health policies and services, but how far that validation actually extends-and how unevenly it is distributed across species-remains an open question. We conducted a systematic review of the scientific literature on the 71 RENISUS species using major bibliographic databases and institutional documents, without language restrictions. Studies were included if they reported pharmacological, toxicological, clinical, or ethnobotanical findings that bear on human health. Records were screened, selected, and mapped to each species, and plants were descriptively classified according to the predominant level of evidence. Five species had sufficient human clinical data to warrant in-depth analysis: Anacardium occidentale L. (Anacardiaceae), Ananas comosus (L.) Merr. (Bromeliaceae), Bidens pilosa L. (Asteraceae), Copaifera langsdorffii Desf. (Fabaceae), and Handroanthus impetiginosus (Mart. ex DC.) Mattos (Bignoniaceae). A preliminary database search retrieved 12,450 initial records. After deduplication, 9,070 unique records were screened against eligibility criteria, ultimately yielding 753 articles meeting the inclusion criteria. In vitro and in vivo studies accounted for most of the literature on RENISUS species. Clinical trials, where they exist at all, cover a narrow subset. The five focal species showed promising findings for wound healing, oral mucositis, gynecological conditions, metabolic regulation, and oncological support, alongside safety concerns-namely hepatotoxicity and herb-drug interactions-that, in some cases, should have surfaced in pharmacovigilance before reaching the literature as case reports. RENISUS encompasses a high diversity of medicinal plants with variable degrees of scientific validation. These findings provide a system-wide evidence baseline for the 71 RENISUS species and offer a practical framework for research prioritization, regulatory decision-making, and the evidence-guided incorporation of medicinal plants into the Brazilian Unified Health System.

articles.title: Research advances and clinical management of drug interactions between voriconazole and antituberculosis agents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: When tuberculosis is complicated by fungal infection, voriconazole and antituberculosis drugs may need to be used in combination, and drug interactions can affect efficacy and safety. METHODS: This structured narrative review used a systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) from database inception to May 2026, together with predefined eligibility criteria and evidence stratification. Clinical pharmacokinetic, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), observational, case-report, and case-series studies were eligible as the primary evidence base. Relevant in vitro studies were reviewed only as mechanistic, hypothesis-generating evidence and were not treated as primary clinical evidence. Because of substantial heterogeneity in study design, populations, interventions, pharmacokinetic endpoints, and reporting completeness, the findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. The direction and potential clinical significance of interactions and key considerations for TDM were summarized by evidence type. RESULTS: A total of 2,198 records were identified, and 17 primary clinical studies were included. Most were case reports or small retrospective studies, with limited paired antituberculosis-drug exposure data and clinical outcomes; generalizability is therefore limited. Existing clinical pharmacokinetic evidence is concentrated on rifamycins. Rifampicin markedly reduces voriconazole exposure and its induction may persist after discontinuation, so coadministration should be avoided. Rifapentine can also substantially lower voriconazole concentrations, with interindividual variability in the offset of induction; dose adjustment and re-initiation after withdrawal require serial TDM. Rifabutin has a bidirectional interaction: it can reduce voriconazole exposure, while voriconazole may increase exposure to rifabutin and its active metabolite. Current U.S. voriconazole labeling lists rifabutin coadministration as contraindicated, and rare off-label case experience does not establish it as a safe alternative. For isoniazid, ethambutol, linezolid, and other non-rifamycin agents, available evidence is mechanistic or hypothesis-generating and does not establish causal interactions or justify empirical voriconazole dose adjustment. CONCLUSION: Management should prioritize avoidance of voriconazole coadministration with rifampicin and rifabutin in accordance with current labeling, and avoidance of rifapentine where feasible. If rifapentine exposure cannot be avoided or has recently stopped, serial TDM should guide voriconazole dosing. For non-rifamycin antituberculosis drugs, monitoring should be matched to the suspected risk (exposure variability, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity, or optic, neurologic, or hematologic toxicity) rather than based on unvalidated empirical dose changes.

articles.title: iPSC-derived RPE as a context-of-use defined NAM framework for RPE-centered drug-induced retinal toxicity assessment.
articles.abstract: The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is essential for outer retinal homeostasis and a key target for drug-induced retinal toxicity. However, conventional preclinical models, including immortalized cell lines and animal systems, may incompletely recapitulate human RPE biology because of limited representation of specialized RPE functions and species-specific differences in retinal physiology. Induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RPE (iPSC-RPE) has emerged as a candidate human-relevant platform for New Approach Methodology (NAM) development, with the potential to improve mechanistic relevance by reproducing key structural and functional features of native human RPE. Its translational utility depends on a clearly defined context of use (COU), reproducible differentiation and functional characterization, and benchmark-based frameworks for future assay qualification and validation. This review evaluates the potential of iPSC-RPE as a COU-defined NAM framework for RPE-centered drug-induced retinal toxicity, with particular emphasis on toxicities in which RPE dysfunction represents a primary or mechanistically important component. We summarize differentiation strategies and critical quality attributes that may inform future assay qualification, evaluate disease-modeling evidence supporting physiological relevance, and discuss applications in ocular safety assessment, including chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine-, MEK inhibitor-, and anti-VEGF-associated retinal effects. We further discuss limitations, including cellular immaturity, donor-to-donor variability, incomplete microenvironmental modeling, and the limited validation of long-term exposure paradigms. Current evidence supports mechanistic concordance for selected RPE-centered toxicities, whereas prospective predictive performance across diverse compounds and clinically relevant exposure conditions remains to be established. Further COU-specific qualification and prospective validation will be required to establish the reliability and decision relevance of iPSC-RPE for defined ocular toxicology applications.

articles.title: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics testing in clinical practice: A pilot implementation in Singapore.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics (PPGx) testing holds promise for optimizing drug therapy, but uptake remains limited in Asia. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of PPGx uptake into clinical practice and its impact on prescribing in an Asian healthcare setting. METHODS: A prospective, multicentre pilot study was conducted to pre-emptively genotype 16 pharmacogenes. Results were integrated into electronic health records, alongside deployment of clinical decision support (CDS) tools for 31 drug-gene pairs. A pharmacogenomics drug information service and digital platforms were also developed. RESULTS: All 2492 participants carried ≥1 actionable variant (median: 5, range: 1-11). Across four institutions within one cluster, 1046 out of 2238 (46.7%) patients were prescribed ≥1 drug with pharmacogenetic association, and of those, 460 (44%) had genotypes linked to undesirable drug responses. Among 285 interruptive CDS alerts, 69 (24.2%) led to prescription modifications. Acceptance was higher for new prescriptions (50.0% vs. 17.3%, p < 0.001), in outpatient settings (31.0% vs. 7.3%, p < 0.001) and among consultants (57.1% vs. other designations 5-27.3%, p < 0.001). The drug information service received 137 enquiries, while 471 and 151 patients accessed the app and web-based platforms respectively. CONCLUSIONS: PPGx testing and genotype-guided prescribing are feasible in Singapore. Widespread adoption requires leadership support, robust informatics infrastructure, clinician engagement and sustainable funding.

articles.title: Renal Function-Guided Valganciclovir Dosing and Ganciclovir Exposure Variability: A Population Pharmacokinetic Simulation Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ganciclovir (GCV) exposure after standard valganciclovir (VGCV) prophylaxis is highly variable. Guidelines recommend Cockcroft-Gault for renal dose adjustment. We evaluated whether Cockcroft-Gault-based dosing achieves the target prophylactic exposure (AUC0-24h: 40-60 mg.h/L) and whether MDRD or CKD-EPI alters exposure. METHODS: Using a validated population pharmacokinetic model, we simulated 10 000 adult solid organ transplant recipients. VGCV doses were assigned according to SmPC renal function categories based on Cockcroft-Gault, MDRD or CKD-EPI. Patient reclassification, target attainment and exposure around dosing thresholds (25, 40 and 60 mL/min) were assessed. RESULTS: MDRD and CKD-EPI reclassified 45.1% and 39.9% of patients, mostly downward, lowering target attainment (20.1% and 22.7% vs. 30.8% with Cockcroft-Gault). Target attainment never exceeded 40% in any category, and underexposure predominated, reaching up to 94.1% in the most impaired renal function categories. Target attainment was consistently lower just below each threshold, and the 25 and 40 mL/min thresholds were set above the renal function ranges where the corresponding regimens achieved target exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Renal function category-based VGCV dosing does not reliably achieve target GCV exposure. Current thresholds are poorly aligned with the exposure-response relationship and warrant re-examination. Alternative equations do not reduce the variability, supporting exposure-guided approaches such as therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing.

articles.title: Spotlight commentary: Redefining drug evaluation in pregnancy: Integrating PBPK modelling and real-world data.
Acute nociceptive stimulation induces long-lasting constitutive activity of spinal μ-opioid receptors that masks pain sensitization.
articles.abstract: Acute nociceptive stimuli evoke transient pain sensitization that normally resolves after the stimulus has ceased. However, whether this apparent recovery reflects restoration of the nociceptive system to its basal state or active suppression of persistent sensitization remains unclear. Here, we show that mechanical hypersensitivity induced by acute chemical or electrical stimulation of primary afferent C-fibers was transient in wild-type mice but persisted for 1-2 weeks in mice lacking spinal μ-opioid receptors (MORs). Furthermore, intrathecal pretreatment with naloxone, naltrexone, or CTOP, all of which act as MOR inverse agonists, prevented recovery from C-fiber-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, whereas the neutral antagonist 6β-naltrexol had no effect. The naltrexone-induced reinstatement of mechanical hypersensitivity was prevented by 6β-naltrexol, consistent with induction of constitutively active spinal MORs. C-fiber stimulation also increased phosphorylation of spinal MORs, a biochemical marker of receptor activation, and this increase was abolished by naltrexone but not by 6β-naltrexol. Although mice had fully recovered behaviorally by 3, 6, and 24 hr after C-fiber stimulation, pharmacological inhibition of constitutively active MORs at each time-point consistently reinstated mechanical hypersensitivity. Together, these findings support a model in which acute nociceptive stimulation induces two parallel forms of long-term spinal plasticity: persistent pain sensitization and constitutive activation of MORs, the latter continuously masking the former to maintain an apparently resolved pain state. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized homeostatic mechanism underlying pain resolution after acute nociceptive stimulation, and the C-fiber-mediated mechanisms for inducing MOR constitutive activity may provide a clue to develop a therapeutic strategy for sustained analgesia.

articles.title: An Industrial Data-Calibrated Mechanistic Modelling Framework for Robust Operation and QbD Design-Space Analysis in Pharmaceutical Fluid-Bed Drying.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Process digitalization through high-fidelity modelling is increasingly used to support Quality by Design (QbD) and Operational Excellence in pharmaceutical manufacturing. In this study, an industrial data-calibrated mechanistic modelling framework was developed for an industrial pharmaceutical batch fluid bed drying process, integrating a mechanistic model calibrated using real industrial data. The objective was not only to predict final moisture content, but also to characterise process dynamics and the effects of key process parameters, transforming the validated model into a decision-support tool for defining robust operating regions within a QbD framework. METHODS: The mechanistic core incorporated two-phase fluidisation hydrodynamics, granular moisture diffusion and convective heat transfer, while model parameters were calibrated using data from eight full-scale industrial batches and evaluated using four independent batches. The validated framework enabled virtual experimentation across inlet air temperature, airflow rate and drying time, together with Monte Carlo-based uncertainty propagation. RESULTS: Validation against four independent batches showed agreement for final residual moisture within the experimentally represented range, with a root mean square error of approximately 0.3% on a wet basis. Simulation results revealed nonlinear interactions among critical process parameters and identified operating regions satisfying residual moisture criteria while maintaining favourable relative energy-performance conditions. Monte Carlo-based uncertainty propagation showed that central operating regions exhibited lower sensitivity to disturbances, whereas boundary conditions amplified variability in critical quality attributes. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the framework extends mechanistic process simulation towards probabilistic design-space construction and risk-informed decision support in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

articles.title: A Novel Sedative Remimazolam Besylate Inhibits Human Lung Cancer Growth in vitro and in vivo.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anaesthetic drugs used during the perioperative period may influence surgical outcomes in cancer patients. Recently, remimazolam besylate, a rapid-onset and ultra-short-acting sedative, has been introduced for sedation and anaesthesia maintenance. This study aimed to assess its potential anti-cancer effects on human lung carcinoma cells (A549) in vitro and in vivo, and to explore the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Cultured A549 lung cancer cells were exposed to remimazolam besylate (0.1 to 500 μM) for up to 24 hours and their viability was assessed with the CCK-8 assay. The effects of remimazolam besylate on cancer cell proliferation, migration, mitochondrial mass, and apoptosis were assessed through RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence staining. Tumour growth was evaluated in a xenograft model of Balb/c nude mice after treatment with 5 mg/kg of remimazolam besylate via intraperitoneal injection for 21 consecutive days. Its cytotoxicity was also assessed with cultured HK-2 normal kidney cells. RESULTS: Remimazolam besylate significantly inhibited cell viability at 200 μM (61.2 ± 12.7 vs 103.8 ± 6.0, P = 0.003) and 300 μM (46 ± 10 vs 95 ± 21, P = 0.02). It suppressed migration (56.38 ± 3.06 vs 85.10 ± 10.84, P = 0.03) and reduced mitochondrial mass (63.5 ± 24.9 vs 150.5 ± 55.9, P = 0.02). Additionally, it increased caspase-3 and cleaved caspase-9 expression, and reduced tumour size by 74.6% compared to the control (P = 0.002). The 50% concentration of cytotoxicity (IC50) for remimazolam besylate in A549 cells was found to be 297.5 μM, whereas the IC50 for HK-2 cells was predicted to be significantly higher at 2,200 μM. CONCLUSION: Remimazolam besylate primarily and preferentially inhibits human lung carcinoma cells. It induces apoptosis associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress and cell death signaling pathways.

articles.title: The PDE4 inhibitor tanimilast (CHF6001) activates CFTR function in native and in F508del-expressing airway epithelial cells.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a disorder caused by mutations in the CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, which result in impaired expression and function of the channel that is regulated by cAMP intracellular levels. Therefore, cAMP-elevating agents have been investigated for the treatment of CF, including phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitors that act by preventing its degradation by PDE enzymes. Here we characterized the effects of the novel inhaled PDE4 inhibitor, tanimilast (CHF6001), designed to overcome PDE inhibitors systemic adverse effects, on CFTR activation by measuring short-circuit current (Isc) in cellular models expressing native and F508del CFTR (CFBE41o- and normal human bronchial epithelial cells: MucilAir™). Various PDE4 genes (PDE4A, B, D) are expressed in both cell models to different extents. Tanimilast was able to increase Isc in a concentration-dependent manner in both cell models, peaking at 0.2 μM in MucilAir™ expressing either WT and F508del CFTR corrected with a combination of VX445 and VX661 for 24 h. Taken together, these results indicate for the first time that the PDE4 inhibitor tanimilast could enhance, in vitro, the effects of CFTR correctors used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Activation of Kv7 Potassium Channels by Sodium New Houttuyfonate Underlies Potent Analgesia in Chronic Pain.
articles.abstract: Activation of voltage-gated Kv7 potassium channels represents an attractive therapeutic strategy for chronic pain. Through network pharmacology screening, Sodium New houttuyfonate (SNH) was identified as a candidate interacting with pain-related targets. This study investigated the analgesic effects and underlying mechanisms of SNH in chronic pain. Using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings on CHO cells expressing Kv7.2/Kv7.3 channels, we found that SNH potentiated Kv7.2/Kv7.3 currents in a concentration-dependent manner (EC50 = 6.6 μM, 95% CI: 2.3 to 9.9 μM) and shifted the voltage-dependent activation curve toward hyperpolarization. Notably, the synergistic effect between its hydrophobic hydrocarbon chain and hydrophilic sulfoacetate group forms the structural basis for the efficient activation of Kv7.2/Kv7.3 currents. SNH was confirmed to potently activate all Kv7.1-Kv7.5 channel subtypes. Furthermore, SNH (100 μM) significantly enhanced the M-current, thereby reducing the excitability of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons from spared nerve injury (SNI) model mice. In mouse models of chronic pain, intraperitoneal administration of SNH markedly increased mechanical paw withdrawal thresholds and thermal withdrawal latencies. In conclusion, our results demonstrate that SNH exerts its antinociceptive effects primarily by activating Kv7 channels, offering a potential for treating neuronal hyperexcitability disorders such as chronic pain.

articles.title: EUK-134, a superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, inhibits inflammatory cytokines, reduces myocyte necroptosis and improves left ventricular remodeling and function in heart failure after myocardial infarction in mice.
articles.abstract: Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a crucial role in heart failure after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood.
