In this study, we investigated whether EUK-134, a synthetic superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, reduces myocardial oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines and myocyte necroptosis and apoptosis, leading to the improvement of left ventricular (LV) remodeling and function in heart failure after MI. Eight-week old C57BL/6J mice underwent MI or sham operation. The animals were randomized to receive EUK-134 (25 mg/kg, every other day, i.p.) or placebo for four weeks. In the MI placebo group, LV end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions were increased, LV fractional shortening and LV ejection fraction were decreased, and these alterations were attenuated by the treatment of EUK-134. In the MI placebo group, myocardial expression of 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine, a marker of oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β and interleukin-6, and phosphorylated RIP1 (p-RIP1), p-RIP3 and p-MLKL, reflective of their respect kinase activities, markers of necroptosis, pro-apoptotic Bax protein, phosphorylated JNK (p-JNK) protein, cleaved caspase protein and myocyte apoptosis were markedly increased, and the increases were prevented by the treatment of EUK-134. Similarly, intracellular levels of ROS, necroptosis and apoptosis were increased in H9C2 cardiomyocytes under mimic ischemia and the increases were prevented by the EUK-134 treatment. These findings suggest that the superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic EUK-134 prevents RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated myocyte necroptosis and Bax/JNK-mediated myocyte apoptosis through inhibition of myocardial oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines, leading to the improvement of post-MI LV remodeling and failure.

articles.title: Targeting Vasopressin Signaling in Sepsis: Effects of Tolvaptan on Inflammation and Aquaporin Dysregulation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection, leading to multiple organ injury. Disturbances in fluid homeostasis and inflammation play key roles in its pathophysiology. Aquaporins, which regulate water transport across cell membranes, may contribute to sepsis-associated organ injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of the vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist tolvaptan on sepsis-induced multiple organ injury and its relationship with aquaporins. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An experimental sepsis model was established in rats using LPS. The animals were divided into control, sepsis, and sepsis + tolvaptan treatment groups. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels, as well as aquaporin-2 (AQP2) and aquaporin-5 (AQP5) expression levels, were evaluated in blood and tissue samples. In addition, histopathological examinations were performed. Furthermore, the effects of tolvaptan on cytotoxicity and inflammatory response were investigated in an in vitro model of LPS-induced inflammation. RESULTS: LPS-induced inflammation was associated with significant elevations in TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels, along with marked reductions in lung AQP5 and kidney AQP2 expression. Tolvaptan treatment significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, increased AQP5 expression, and further enhanced the reduction in AQP2 expression. Histopathological evaluations confirmed the organ-protective effects of tolvaptan. CONCLUSION: Tolvaptan attenuated the inflammatory response and alleviated organ injury associated with sepsis. The observed increase in AQP5 expression and suppression of AQP2 expression suggest that vasopressin V2 receptor inhibition may modulate aquaporin expression and contribute to protection against sepsis-induced organ injury. Therefore, the vasopressin V2 receptor-aquaporin axis may represent a potential therapeutic target in the treatment of sepsis.

articles.title: The role of surface energy in dry powders for inhalation: When does it matter?
articles.abstract: Although adhesive mixtures are widely used in inhalation therapy, mechanisms governing their dispersion are still not fully understood. This study investigates whether the reduction in surface energy leads to changes in dispersion behaviour or whether the relationship described in the literature is an artefact. Carrier particles with reduced roughness were produced by controlled crystallisation, and smooth, spherical active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) particles were engineered by spray drying. Commercial API and inhalation-grade lactose were also used as 'rough' standards. Carrier particles were tested in unmodified and silanised forms, the latter exhibiting reduced surface energy. Adhesion behaviour was assessed by atomic force microscopy (AFM), and formulations combining the different carrier and API grades were evaluated for aerodynamic performance. For commercial-grade, non-ideal particles, surface-energy alterations did not readily translate into differences in aerodynamic performance. In contrast, for engineered smooth particles, reduced surface energy altered practical adhesion and improved aerodynamic performance significantly. These findings support the view that detachment of rough particles is primarily governed by lateral forces and friction, whereas fundamental adhesion governs detachment of smooth particles. Aerodynamic performance improvements previously attributed to surface-energy modification, including through leucine or magnesium stearate, should therefore be critically reconsidered. The utility of surface energy as a predictive tool for aerodynamic performance of adhesive mixtures is only appropriate if other influencing parameters, that is roughness, are carefully considered in the interpretation.

articles.title: Optical coherence tomography as a process analytical technology for oral film formulations.
articles.abstract: In oral film manufacturing, the dose of the active pharmaceutical ingredient is set by cutting the cast film into portions of defined area, which makes film thickness a critical quality attribute and an attractive target for calibration-free in-process measurement. This study evaluated Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) to monitor film thickness of oral films along the offline-to-inline continuum. A galvanometer-scanning spectral-domain OCT system, acquiring full two-dimensional cross-sections, was applied offline to cast films and inline above the moving, dried film of a continuous coating line. An OSeeT Pharma 1D sensor, which acquires depth profiles at a fixed lateral position and evaluates the interfaces within the instrument, was operated on a custom-built conveying bench reproducing continuous film movement. Offline, OCT resolved internal defects, including air bubbles, insoluble inclusions and the interlayer boundary of bilayer films. Preliminary observations further indicated its potential to detect storage-related microstructural changes. OCT consistently yielded higher thickness values than a manually operated micrometer screw, with potential contributing factors, including film compression during contact measurement and the assumption of a constant refractive index, being discussed. Inline, thickness variations induced by deliberate variation of pump rate, coating knife height and liner speed were resolved for three different polymeric film formers, with thickness values extracted by post-processing of the recorded cross-sections, although evaluable frames were lost wherever the moving film left the set focal range. The OSeeT sensor returned stable thickness, roughness and homogeneity along the entire film length and reproduced the same systematic offset against the micrometer screw reference, delivering these values continuously and without post-processing. Structural information therefore remains available alongside continuous monitoring if the acquisition is configured to retain it. The main obstacles to the use of OCT as an inline Process Analytical Technology in continuous oral film manufacturing therefore lie in system integration, i.e. mechanical film guidance, automated onboard evaluation and image retention, rather than in the optical performance of the instruments.

articles.title: Quantifying the impact of press deformation on compression kinematics during tableting: An experimentally validated analytical approach.
articles.abstract: Compression speed is a critical parameter for the manufacturing of pharmaceutical tablets. Tableting scale-up often significantly increases compression speeds, frequently resulting in different final tablet characteristics or defects like capping or lamination. For this reason, compaction simulators are widely utilized to emulate the punch displacement cycles of production-scale rotary presses. While conventional simulator cycles rely on theoretical equations derived strictly from the geometric features of rotary equipment, they neglect structural frame compliance, which considerably alters the true velocity profile during tableting. The present work introduces a novel, universally applicable analytical methodology to calculate the actual, deformation-compensated compression speed by accounting for the deformation of the press and the compressibility of the tablet formulation. The method was experimentally validated against empirical punch kinematics during the loading phase on an instrumented compaction simulator. The model was then applied to a production-scale rotary press, quantitatively demonstrating that structural machine deformation reduces the actual compression velocity to nearly half of the theoretical value near peak force. The proposed method relies entirely on data readily determined in standard development and manufacturing environments, providing a highly practical tool for aligning compaction simulator profiles with production equipment, optimizing process scale-up, and troubleshooting compression speed-related production challenges.

articles.title: Female ddY mice show a weaker diazepam-induced reduction in aggressive biting behavior toward inanimate objects and lower hypothalamic KCC2 expression than males do.
articles.abstract: Anyone may engage in aggressive behavior under the influence of stress. Animal models have been used to elucidate the mechanisms underlying aggression. Herein, we studied aggressive behavior in chronically isolation-reared male and female mice using an Aggressive Response Meter (ARM) device. The ARM device induces aggressive biting behavior (ABB) in mice toward inanimate objects, and measures its intensity and frequency, hereafter referred to as ABB intensity and ABB frequency, respectively. We characterized ABB intensity and frequency compared with open field test (OFT), social interaction test, and elevated plus maze (EPM). ABB intensity and frequency were increased and the time in the center zone in OFT was decreased in isolation-reared male and female mice compared with group-reared counterparts. No statistically significant correlation was detected between ABB intensity and other behavioral features in OFT, social interaction test, and EPM, indicating that ABB intensity reflects behavioral characteristics not fully explained by these behavioral characteristics. As the effects of GABA-targeting agents are poorly characterized, we examined the effect of diazepam on ABB. At higher doses (4 mg/kg), diazepam effectively reduced ABB levels in both males and females, with males showing higher sensitivity than females at lower doses (2 mg/kg). The number of c-Fos-expressing cells in the dmVMH and dlPAG was high in mice with high ABB. We next analyzed KCC2, a K+-Cl- co-transporter that maintains inhibitory GABA transmission. Low KCC2 expression in the hypothalamus of female was detected using qPCR and immunoblotting. Testosterone supplementation enhanced female responsiveness to diazepam at lower doses.

articles.title: Rapid performance validation testing of an intraoperatively customizable antibiotic-eluting resorbable bone graft implant targeting prosthetic joint infection.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) present a major clinical challenge, for which prolonged, localized antibiotic delivery to eradicate infection are routinely pursued to facilitate bone regeneration while minimizing systemic toxicity. Current treatments, such as antibiotic-loaded polymethylmethacrylate bone cements, are non-resorbable and provide inconsistent antibiotic release. This study evaluates release of antibiotics from a novel, FDA-cleared, biphasic, synthetic, resorbable bone graft device composed of calcium carbonate and hydroxyapatite bound with polycaprolactone and polylactic-co-glycolic acid. This bone graft device can be intraoperatively mixed with patient-specific antibiotics (e.g., tobramycin and/or vancomycin) to form drug-loaded granules for implantation into bone voids. Drugs release completely from this formulation in 6-8 weeks. To rapidly screen and assess drug release consistency from these commercial formulations, a United States Pharmacopeia (USP) compendial dissolution method was employed, showing ∼ 100% tobramycin release within 145 min from this drug-loaded device. We then compared this rapid release to previously published actual 8-week release data and predictions from Weibull and Siepmann models fit to the published 8-week data. Results validate the utility of the rapid USP compendial dissolution method as a valuable, accelerated surrogate predictor for the previously published device-controlled antimicrobial release in vivo of over 6 weeks. These findings produce a practical quality control assay for two FDA-cleared implant platforms, one currently in clinical trials for targeted treatment of PJIs and other orthopedic infections where infection control and bone healing must be simultaneously addressed locally. This approach facilitates performance verification of an intraoperatively customizable, antibiotic-eluting, resorbable bone graft device with controlled, localized delivery of therapeutically relevant antibiotics that also supports new bone formation.

articles.title: Anhydroicaritin Ameliorates iNKT Cell-Mediated Hepatitis by Disrupting Immune- Hepatocyte Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The Bushen formula (BSF) is a traditional Chinese herbal prescription widely used to treat viral hepatitis B, a condition where natural killer T (NKT) cell hyperactivation has been reported to trigger immune-mediated liver injury and fibrosis. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic potential of BSF and its key natural ingredients in mitigating NKT cell activation-mediated liver injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A preclinical model of iNKT cell-mediated hepatitis was established in mice by intravenous injection of α-Galactosylceramide (α-GalCer). The potential active ingredients were identified by using Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography-Quadrupole-Time of Flight Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF/MS) and functional assays. RESULTS: BSF treatment significantly alleviated iNKT cell-mediated hepatitis in mice as evidenced by decreased liver injury and inflammatory markers with noticeable downregulation of serum and hepatic levels of TNF-α and CXCL1, both of which are key factors contributing to iNKT cell-mediated liver injury. By performing UPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis of BSF, we identified anhydroicaritin (AHI) as an important anti-inflammatory ingredient of BSF, based on its remarkable ability to inhibit CXCL1 production in hepatocytes stimulated by TNF-α. Mechanistically, AHI inhibited the TNF-α downstream signaling pathway JNK-AP-1 in hepatocytes, thereby limiting CXCL1 production and neutrophil infiltration. Additionally, AHI directly attenuated iNKT activation and its TNF-α production. CONCLUSION: AHI prevents iNKT-mediated hepatitis by inhibiting two key pathways: it suppresses iNKT-mediated TNF-α production and blocks TNF-α from inducing CXCL1 production in hepatocytes. This dual action ultimately prevents neutrophil infiltration, serving as a key mechanism behind the therapeutic benefits of BSF in treating viral hepatitis B.

articles.title: Gastrodin Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Depressive-Like Phenotypes via Modulation of the PHD2-HIF-1α/Glycolysis Axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gastrodia elata is commonly used in traditional Chinese medicine to calm the spirit, soothe the liver, and relieve depression, primarily treating central emotional disorders such as low mood and irritability caused by emotional imbalances. Our previous research has confirmed that its main active component, gastrodin, can prevent and treat Alzheimer's disease by alleviating neuroinflammation. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic effect and molecular mechanism of GAS on inflammatory depression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A classic LPS-induced mouse model of inflammatory depression was established, and model mice were subjected to continuous intervention with gradient doses of GAS to explore dose-dependent therapeutic effects. Multiple behavioral paradigms were applied to comprehensively evaluate depressive-like behaviors, while cortical histopathological staining was performed to assess neuronal injury and brain tissue lesions. High-throughput multi-omic screening and single-cell transcriptomic profiling were further utilized to screen key functional genes, metabolic pathways, and microglial phenotypic alterations. Combined with HIF-1α pharmacological rescue experiments, the core molecular pathway mediated by GAS was systematically verified. RESULTS: Behavioral and pathological detection results confirmed that GAS treatment significantly and dose-dependently relieved LPS-induced depressive-like behaviors and alleviated neuronal damage and structural lesions in the prefrontal cortex. Network pharmacology and untargeted metabolomics indicated that gastrodin modulates HIF-1α-related pathways. Single-cell analyses further highlighted the critical role of microglia, with elevated Egln1 (PHD2) transcript abundance specifically detected in surveillance microglia. Mechanistic assays further validated that GAS markedly upregulated PHD2 activity, which facilitated the ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HIF-1α, thereby effectively reversing neuroinflammation-triggered aberrant cerebral glycolysis and potentially contributing to the restoration of brain metabolic homeostasis. CONCLUSIONS: GAS alleviates inflammatory depression by modulating the PHD2-HIF-1α-glycolysis axis in a microglial subtype-dependent manner, providing a novel targeted strategy for inflammatory depression.

articles.title: Xiaoyaosan ameliorates depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction: insights into gut-brain fluid metabolism and aldosterone/MR-related signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The co-occurrence of depression and gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction presents a clinical challenge, as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like sertraline frequently exacerbate gastrointestinal adverse symptoms. Xiaoyaosan, a classic Chinese prescription, simultaneously alleviates both domains, yet its underlying its dual-target efficacy remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the effects of Xiaoyaosan on depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction, with particular emphasis on their associations with fluid metabolism-related alterations and aldosterone/MR signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) -induced depressed rat model was employed. We evaluated depression-like behaviors, fluid metabolism phenotypes, colonic transcriptomics, and performed targeted molecular analyses on colonic and hippocampal tissues. RESULTS: At the tested dose, Xiaoyaosan improved depression-like behaviors and several gastrointestinal and fluid metabolism-related parameters in CUMS-exposed rats. Although both XYS and sertraline alleviated depression-like behaviors, distinct effects on gastrointestinal functional indicators were observed under the volume-matched administration conditions. Colonic transcriptomic analysis revealed gene expression changes associated with aldosterone-related signaling. XYS treatment reduced circulating aldosterone and corticosterone levels, improved serum electrolyte profiles and colonic barrier-associated indicators, and decreased MR expression in the colon and hippocampus. These changes were accompanied by increased hippocampal AQP4 mRNA expression, improved ATPase activities, and attenuated neuroinflammatory responses. Correlation analyses further revealed associations among these molecular alterations and behavioral parameters. CONCLUSION: Using integrated behavioral, gastrointestinal, transcriptomic, and molecular analyses, this study provides novel experimental evidence linking the beneficial effects of XYS on depression-like behaviors and gastrointestinal dysfunction to coordinated alterations in fluid metabolism-related indicators and aldosterone/MR signaling, offering a fresh mechanistic perspective on gut-brain regulatory effects of XYS.

articles.title: ZeXieYin Formula Attenuates Trimethylamine N-Oxide-Induced Cognitive Impairment via Modulating ZBP1-Associated PANoptotic Signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: ZeXieYin Formula (ZXYF), a classical prescription recorded in Huangdi Neijing, has been prescribed for centuries to invigorate the spleen, drain dampness, and transform phlegm to resolve metabolic fluid stagnation and mental clouding (Maoxuan). In traditional Chinese medicine theory, the accumulation of pathological phlegm-dampness obstructing cerebral orifices (Tan Meng Shen Qiao) represents a primary etiology of cognitive decline, conceptually aligning with modern metabolic endotoxemia induced by gut-derived trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO). Although ZXYF alleviates TMAO-induced cognitive deficits, its central neuroprotective mechanisms remain poorly defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether ZXYF protects against TMAO-induced hippocampal neuronal injury and cognitive impairment by suppressing Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1)-associated PANoptotic signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The standardized aqueous extract of ZXYF was chemically profiled using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-HRMS. In vivo, mice were chronically exposed to TMAO via drinking water and treated with ZXYF (3.25 or 6.5 g/kg/day). Cognitive performance was evaluated using open field, Y-maze, novel object recognition, and Morris water maze tests. Hippocampal neuronal survival and mitochondrial ultrastructure were examined by NeuN immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy. In vitro, murine hippocampal HT-22 cells were challenged with TMAO and treated with ZXYF. Cytotoxicity, apoptosis, ZBP1 expression, PANoptotic effectors, and PANoptosome assembly (ASC/CASP8/RIPK3 colocalization) were analyzed using live-cell imaging, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: ZXYF dose-dependently ameliorated TMAO-induced deficits in spatial learning, working memory, and object recognition without altering spontaneous locomotion or anxiety-like behavior. ZXYF attenuated pyramidal neuronal loss in hippocampal CA1 and CA3 subfields and reversed mitochondrial vacuolar degeneration. In hippocampal tissues, ZXYF downregulated ZBP1 expression, pro-apoptotic caspases (CASP3/8/9), phosphorylated MLKL, active Caspase-1, and cleaved GSDMD/GSDME. In HT-22 cells, ZXYF reduced TMAO-induced cell death and apoptosis, suppressed ZBP1-dependent PANoptotic cascades, and prevented ASC/CASP8/RIPK3 aggregation and colocalization. CONCLUSIONS: ZXYF mitigates TMAO-induced cognitive impairment and hippocampal neuronal injury in experimental models, effects accompanied by the preservation of mitochondrial integrity, reduced ZBP1 expression, and attenuation of PANoptosis-related molecular changes. These findings provide experimental support for the traditional application of ZXYF in dispelling phlegm-dampness to unblock the orifices of the mind (Tan Meng Shen Qiao), highlighting its potential as an ethnopharmacological multi-target formulation against metabolic neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Chaihuang Qingfu Pills attenuate severe acute pancreatitis-associated acute lung injury by restoring efferocytosis via the NF-κB/CD47 axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chaihuang Qingfu Pills (CHQF), a traditional Chinese medicine formulation derived from the classical Qingyi Decoction, have long been used in clinical practice for severe acute pancreatitis (SAP). Our previous study demonstrated that CHQF reduces SAP-associated acute lung injury (SAP-ALI) clinically and protects against it experimentally; however, the mechanisms underlying its effects in the early stage of the disease remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the protective effects of CHQF against early SAP-ALI and to elucidate the mechanisms by which CHQF modulates efferocytosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An L-arginine-induced SAP mouse model and an in vitro coculture system of pancreatic acinar and alveolar epithelial cells were used. Early-stage (6 h) lung proteomics was integrated with serum pharmacochemical profiling and network pharmacology, and the findings were validated by histopathological analysis, immunofluorescence and TUNEL staining, flow cytometry, Western blotting, ChIP-qPCR, molecular docking and pharmacological intervention. RESULTS: CHQF improved survival and attenuated pancreatic and lung injury in SAP mice. Early-stage proteomics revealed broad disturbances of efferocytosis-related proteins; among them, the cell-surface "don't eat me" signal CD47 was markedly upregulated in SAP lung tissue and on apoptotic alveolar epithelial cells, accompanied by impaired efferocytosis, and these alterations were reversed by CHQF. Functionally, blockade of CD47 significantly enhanced the engulfment of apoptotic cells, establishing CD47 as a negative regulator of this process. Mechanistically, CHQF inhibited IKK-β/NF-κB pathway activation and the binding of NF-κB to the CD47 promoter, thereby suppressing CD47 transcription, as confirmed by pharmacological modulation of NF-κB in vitro. CONCLUSIONS: CHQF protects against early SAP-ALI by targeting the IKK-β-NF-κB-CD47 axis to restore efferocytosis. These findings support the clinical potential of this classical formulation and highlight efferocytosis as a druggable process in inflammatory lung injury.

articles.title: Propranolol disrupts fear-induced persistent cocaine place preference and unmasks an aversion component.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and cocaine use disorder frequently co-occur, but how traumatic memories influence drug-associated behavior during drug withdrawal is unclear. We combined traumatic-like conditioned fear memory recall (FR) with cocaine-induced conditioned place preference (CPP) in male mice, and tested preference repeatedly during withdrawal, with or without prior FR sessions. The effects of the β-adrenergic antagonist propranolol and the CRF-R1 antagonist antalarmin administered before each FR and before fear extinction were also tested. Progressive extinction of CPP occurred along repeated testing sessions in the control condition. In contrast, repeated FRs maintained a stable, persistent preference for the cocaine-associated compartment, accompanied by an increased compulsive-like behavior in the marble burying test, hyperthermia and elevated corticosterone plasma levels. Antalarmin did not prevent the FR-induced persistence of CPP. Cluster analysis revealed instead that propranolol split animals into two subgroups: one subgroup that progressively lost preference and developed even an apparent conditioned place aversion to the cocaine-associated compartment, and another subgroup that maintained and incubated CPP. The divergence toward place aversion was somehow associated with increased conditioned freezing during FRs. Subsequent fear extinction reduced preferences in both propranolol subgroups, indicating a shared dependence on ongoing fear memory engagement. Our findings identify fear memory reactivations as an active regulator of drug-associated motivational states during withdrawal, with a noradrenergic mechanism as a proximal mediator, suggesting that β-adrenergic blockade combined with exposure-based extinction may benefit comorbid PTSD and cocaine use disorder.

articles.title: Vasodilatory and antihypertensive effects of sotagliflozin: Ex vivo evaluation in isolated rat aortic rings and an in vivo assessment in spontaneously hypertensive rats.
articles.abstract: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, is noted for its cardioprotective and antihypertensive effects, yet its direct vascular action remains unclear. This study investigated its ex vivo vasodilatory effects in isolated rat thoracic aorta and in vivo antihypertensive effects in non-diabetic Spontaneously Hypertensive rats (SHRs), with subchronic safety assessment. Aortic rings were pre-contracted with phenylephrine or potassium chloride, and underlying mechanisms were studied using pathway-specific inhibitors against matched vehicle controls. Blood pressure and heart rate were measured weekly over 28 days of oral treatment, and safety assessed through body weight, organ weight, biochemistry and hematology. Sotagliflozin induced a concentration-dependent, predominantly endothelium-dependent vasodilation. Cyclooxygenase-derived prostanoid signaling coupled to the AC/cAMP/PKA axis contributed most consistently. In contrast, attenuation by L-NAME and ODQ was surmounted at higher concentrations, indicating a supplementary role for the NO/sGC/cGMP pathway. Vasodilation persisted under KCl-induced depolarization and was unaffected by potassium channel blockers, arguing against a requirement for potassium channel-mediated hyperpolarization. Sotagliflozin also blunted vasoconstriction mediated by voltage-operated calcium channels and inositol triphosphate receptors. In vivo, 200 mg/kg significantly reduced systolic blood pressure relative to baseline and vehicle control, comparably to propranolol and without reflex tachycardia, whereas diastolic and mean arterial pressures were unaltered. Body and organ weights were unaffected, serum uric acid was lower at 50 and 100 mg/kg, urea was higher at the upper doses, and hematology was unremarkable. These findings indicate that sotagliflozin exerts direct vasodilatory activity in the rat thoracic aorta and lowers systolic blood pressure at supratherapeutic doses, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Attentional bias in smokers and e-cigarette users who formerly or currently smoke cigarettes: an eye-tracking study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Dual use of tobacco cigarettes and e-cigarettes has become increasingly common, yet little is known about attentional bias (AB) towards smoking-related cues across patterns of cigarette and e-cigarette use. OBJECTIVES: We examined AB towards smoking-related cues among current and former cigarette smokers with and without e-cigarette use using eye-tracking technology. METHODS: Participants included 62 cigarette smokers, 41 dual users, 26 full-switchers, 61 former smokers, and 65 non-using controls. AB was assessed using a free-viewing eye-tracking task and calculated as the difference in mean relative fixation time between smoking-related and neutral images. Group differences were examined using age-adjusted ANCOVA, and associations with baseline smoking and vaping craving were examined using linear regression. RESULTS: Cigarette smokers and dual users exhibited significantly greater AB towards smoking-related cues than former smokers and non-using controls (p ≤ 0.022). Full-switchers exhibited greater AB than non-using controls (p = 0.004), but did not significantly differ from former smokers. AB did not significantly differ among cigarette smokers, dual users, and full-switchers. Smoking craving was positively associated with AB among cigarette smokers and dual users, with a significantly stronger association among dual users (interaction p = 0.020). Although the group × vaping craving interaction was not significant (p = 0.145), vaping craving was positively associated with AB in a model excluding the interaction term (p = 0.016). CONCLUSIONS: Smoking-related AB was evident among dual users and individuals who had completely switched from cigarettes to e-cigarettes. Former smokers exhibited AB comparable to non-using controls, consistent with the possibility that neuroadaptations underlying smoking cue salience may weaken following sustained abstinence.

articles.title: GABA regulation of dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens is sexually dimorphic and changed by cocaine exposure.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) core is shaped by local inhibitory microcircuits, yet whether this regulation differs between sexes remains unknown. OBJECTIVES: Here, we investigated sex differences in GABA-A and GABA-B receptor regulation of dopamine release in the NAc core and determined whether these mechanisms are altered by repeated cocaine exposure. METHODS: Using ex vivo fast-scan cyclic voltammetry, we measured dopamine release in the NAc core of male and female mice following pharmacological manipulation of GABA-A and GABA-B receptors. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing data were analyzed to assess sex differences in GABA receptor subunit expression. Finally, mice received repeated cocaine injections (10 mg/kg, i.p., five consecutive days), and dopamine release regulation by GABA receptors was assessed 24 hours after the final injection. RESULTS: GABA-A and GABA-B receptors exerted distinct, sexually dimorphic control over dopamine release. GABA-B receptor antagonism increased dopamine release in males but not females; GABA-A receptor antagonism produced stronger enhancement of dopamine release in females. These differences were not explained by broad differences in receptor expression or responsiveness to receptor activation, suggesting sex differences in the engagement of local GABAergic circuits. Interestingly, GABA-B regulation occurs indirectly through cholinergic interneurons, whereas GABA-A regulation was independent of cholinergic input, potentially suggesting a more direct mechanism at dopamine axon terminals. Repeated cocaine exposure selectively attenuated GABA-A-dependent modulation in females. CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings identify divergent GABAergic pathways that tune dopamine output across sexes and reveal how cocaine reshapes these microcircuits, offering a mechanistic basis for sex differences in addiction vulnerability.

articles.title: The effect of systemic naloxone administration on diverse conditioned fear behaviors.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Freezing has historically been the primary measure of conditioned fear, despite evidence that defensive behaviors are diverse and sexually dimorphic. Although mu-opioid receptor (MOR) signaling regulates fear learning and conditioned analgesia, its influence on diverse defensive behaviors remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated the effects of systemic MOR antagonism on freezing, darting, shock responsivity, and ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) during fear conditioning and recall in male and female rats. METHODS: Adult male and female Sprague Dawley rats received naloxone (5 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline before auditory fear conditioning consisting of seven tone-shock pairings. Fear recall was assessed 24 hours later through three tone presentations in a novel context. RESULTS: Naloxone produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. During conditioning, naloxone increased baseline and early-tone freezing in males, whereas females exhibited reduced shock-response velocity and increased post-shock freezing. Darting and USV production were not significantly affected. During recall, freezing did not differ between treatment groups. However, naloxone-treated females exhibited fewer alarm callers overall, but increased vocalization among animals that called. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic naloxone differentially modulates defensive behaviors in male and female rats, highlighting sex-dependent effects of opioid receptor antagonism on conditioned fear expression. The dissociation between freezing and alarm calling during recall further suggests that these behaviors may reflect distinct components of fear processing.

articles.title: Restoration of mitophagy by crebanine suppresses sevoflurane-induced microglial activation and cognitive deficits by blocking mitochondrial DNA-triggered cGAS-STING pathway.
articles.abstract: Sevoflurane, a volatile anesthetic in widespread clinical use, is increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of postoperative cognitive dysfunction. Although neuroinflammation driven by microglial activation is a recognized contributor, the upstream mechanisms linking anesthesia to this inflammatory response remain poorly defined. Crebanine, a natural isoquinoline alkaloid with well-known anti-inflammatory properties, remains unexplored for its impact on mitochondrial quality control during anesthetic neurotoxicity. We investigated whether crebanine protects against sevoflurane-induced cognitive deficits by restoring microglial mitophagy and suppressing the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-cGAS-STING pathway. Sevoflurane-exposed BV2 microglial cells and aged rats were employed as in vitro and in vivo models of anesthesia-induced neurotoxicity, respectively. The neuroprotective effects of crebanine were assessed by evaluating cell viability, microglial activation, inflammatory responses, mitophagy, mitochondrial function, hippocampal neuronal morphology, apoptosis, and cognitive deficits. The underlying mechanism was investigated by measuring cytosolic mitochondrial DNA levels and the activation status of the cGAS-STING pathway. In BV2 microglial cells, we found that sevoflurane exposure disrupted mitophagic flux, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, excessive mitochondrial ROS generation, and subsequent leakage of mtDNA into the cytosol. This cytosolic mtDNA triggered the cGAS-STING pathway, driving pro-inflammatory cytokine production and promoting M1-like polarization. Crebanine treatment potently restored mitophagic flux, curtailed mtDNA release, and deactivated the inflammatory cascade, shifting microglia toward an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype. Pharmacological inhibition of mitophagy with 3-MA or direct activation of STING using DMXAA completely abolished the protective effects of crebanine, confirming its neuroprotection depends on this specific pathway. In animal experiments, administration of crebanine to aged male Sprague-Dawley rats markedly attenuated sevoflurane-induced hippocampal neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, ultimately preserving spatial learning and memory function, as assessed by the Morris water maze test. Crebanine exerts its neuroprotective effects by restoring microglial mitophagy, thereby suppressing mtDNA-mediated cGAS-STING signaling and preserving cognitive function. This positions the mitophagy-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis as a viable therapeutic target for managing anesthesia-induced neurocognitive decline.

articles.title: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas unravels renal cell heterogeneity and intercellular communication in Adriamycin-induced nephropathy.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study is to characterize the cellular and transcriptomic landscape of Adriamycin (ADR)-induced renal fibrosis and identify intercellular communication pathways associated with fibrotic progression. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to profile transcriptomic alterations in ADR-induced kidney fibrosis. Differential expression and pathway enrichment analyses were conducted to identify fibrosis-associated molecular programs. CellChat analysis was applied to infer intercellular communication networks. Immunofluorescence and western blot analyses were used to validate macrophage-tubular interactions and SPP1/LAMININ-associated signaling alterations. Cross-species validation was further performed using human kidney datasets from GEO and GTEx. ADR injury profoundly remodeled the renal cellular ecosystem, characterized by depletion of proximal straight tubule (PST) and proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) cells and accumulation of macrophages. Differential expression and pathway analyses revealed a conserved pro-fibrotic transcriptional program enriched in inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related pathways, accompanied by marked upregulation of SPP1 and other fibrogenic mediators. CellChat analysis identified altered intercellular communication networks, particularly between injured tubular epithelial cells and macrophages, which was further supported by immunofluorescence analysis. Increased expression of SPP1, CD44, and LAMININ proteins was validated by western blot analyses. Cross-species comparison was further performed using human kidney transcriptomic datasets from GEO and GTEx to assess the relevance of SPP1/LAMININ-associated expression patterns in human CKD. This study provides an in-depth single-cell atlas of ADR-induced renal fibrosis and identifies putative SPP1- and LAMININ-associated epithelial-macrophage communication signatures that may contribute to fibrotic remodeling. These findings highlight candidate signaling pathways for future mechanistic investigation and therapeutic exploration.

articles.title: Mannosylated nanostructured lipid carriers of thiabendazole against Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung biofilm infection: in vitro and in vivo characterization, with relevance to cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop mannosylated nanostructured lipid carriers loaded with Thiabendazole for intravenous delivery to prevent lung biofilm formation. Mannosylated NLCs combine the targeting capabilities of mannose-functionalized carriers with the favorable physicochemical properties of NLCs. Mannose-coated NLCs (MCT-NLCs), prepared via microemulsification using Glyceryl monostearate, olive oil, and Geraniol, had an approximate size of 240 nm, a zeta potential of about - 32.5 mV, an entrapment efficiency of 96%, and released about 84% of the drug within 24 h. Microscopy showed spherical particles under 250 nm, supported by thermal and diffraction analyses. TEM and IR spectra confirmed surface mannose. In vitro, they demonstrated sustained drug release compared to free drug. After IV administration, these NLCs reduced bacterial counts and minimized lung tissue damage in rats infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa over seven days, demonstrating improved initial in vivo results, though they did not eradicate the infection. This study did not evaluate the formulation's safety, as it is a repurposed work. In vivo, the NLCs significantly lowered bacterial load and inflammation in a rat model of inhaled Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms relevant to cystic fibrosis over seven days, indicating potential to reduce bacterial contamination and tissue damage, although their targeting mechanism and ability to cure were not confirmed.

articles.title: Pharmacogenetic testing to improve care in the emergency department.
articles.abstract: Nearly 20% of emergency department (ED) encounters involve medications with actionable pharmacogenomic (PGx) guidance available, and population-based studies suggest over 90% of patients carry at least one PGx variant potentially affecting drug response. Despite this, PGx testing in emergency medicine remains rare. This perspective summarizes current evidence supporting PGx implementation in the ED, key barriers to integration, and future directions for PGx testing in acute care. Feasibility studies demonstrate that PGx testing can be incorporated into ED workflows. Observational data suggest clinically important associations between CYP2C19 variability and clopidogrel-related bleeding, CYP2D6 metabolism and opioid-related ED visits, and a high prevalence of actionable gene-drug interactions in older adults presenting with falls. In pediatric psychiatric populations, combinatorial PGx testing has been associated with differences in drug exposure and clinical outcomes. However, no randomized controlled trials testing the clinical utility of PGx testing have been conducted in ED populations. Key barriers to implementation include prolonged PGx testing turnaround times, lack of standardized ordering workflows, limited clinician familiarity with PGx interpretation, inconsistent reimbursement, and challenges integrating results into clinical decision support systems. Future priorities should include prospective interventional trials assessing clinical outcomes, targeted implementation focused on high-risk gene-drug pairs, and incorporation of PGx education into emergency medicine training. Although current evidence is largely feasibility-based, the ED represents a potentially high-yield setting for PGx integration given frequent exposure to actionable medications and the high burden of potentially preventable adverse drug events.

articles.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid exhibits antitumor effects and synergistically enhances carboplatin sensitivity in endometrial cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity-related metabolic dysfunction and chronic inflammation are well-established drivers of the carcinogenesis and progression of endometrial cancer (EC). Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) is a long-chain omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid that has previously demonstrated broad anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor properties in various cancer models. In this study, we evaluated the anti-tumorigenic effects of EPA in EC cell lines and in a genetically engineered mouse model of endometrioid EC. METHODS: Human EC cell lines, KLE and HEC-1B, were used to evaluate the effects of EPA alone or in combination with carboplatin on cell proliferation, invasion, cell cycle profile, stress response, and apoptosis. An LKB1 fl/fl p53  fl/fl genetically engineered mouse model of endometrioid EC was used to examine the effects of EPA on endometrial tumor growth. RESULTS: EPA treatment markedly suppressed cell proliferation and colony formation in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, EPA induced G1 cell cycle arrest, promoted cellular stress, and activated cleaved caspases, while inhibiting cell adhesion and migration. These phenotypes were accompanied by robust inhibition of the AKT/mTOR signaling axis and activation of MAPK-mediated stress pathways. Inflammatory signaling was similarly attenuated, as evidenced by reduced TNF-α-induced COX-2 expression and decreased phosphorylation of NF-κB. Importantly, EPA synergized with carboplatin to enhance anti-tumor efficacy. Combination treatment produced stronger suppression of cell proliferation and invasion, increased apoptotic activity, and downregulation of key survival and oncogenic regulators, including phosphorylated AKT, Bcl-2, β-catenin, and CDK4. Four weeks of EPA administration significantly reduced endometrial tumor burden in both obese and lean mice, accompanied by decreased expression of Ki-67, Bcl-xL, β-catenin, and COX-2 in endometrial tumor tissues. CONCLUSION: EPA exerts potent anti-tumor activity in EC through coordinated modulation of oncogenic signaling, inflammatory pathways, cellular stress responses, and apoptosis. Moreover, its ability to enhance carboplatin sensitivity highlights the potential of EPA as an adjuvant therapeutic candidate for EC and warrants further investigation in preclinical models of EC.

articles.title: Simultaneous determination of osimertinib and almonertinib concentrations in human plasma and cerebrospinal fluid using UPLC-MS/MS method and its clinical applications.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to establish a sensitive analytical method to simultaneously measure concentrations of two third-generation EGFR inhibitors, osimertinib and almonertinib, in human plasma and cerebrospinal fluid. A further objective was to investigate the relationship between these drug concentrations, their penetration into the central nervous system, and clinical treatment efficacy in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with brain metastases. METHODS: An ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed and fully validated for the simultaneous quantification of osimertinib and almonertinib. Plasma and cerebrospinal fluid samples were collected from twenty NSCLC patients with brain metastases (7 receiving osimertinib, 13 receiving almonertinib) at steady-state trough concentration. Drug concentrations were measured, and blood-brain barrier penetration rates were calculated (cerebrospinal fluid/plasma concentration ratio × 100%). Treatment efficacy was assessed via lung CT and brain MRI using RECIST criteria. RESULTS: The validated UPLC-MS/MS method demonstrated excellent sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for both drugs in both matrices. Significant inter-individual variability was observed in plasma concentrations, cerebrospinal fluid concentrations, and penetration rates. For both drugs, steady-state plasma concentration showed no significant correlation with lung tumor response. However, higher cerebrospinal fluid concentration and penetration rate were positively correlated with improved treatment efficacy for brain metastases, as evidenced by better outcomes on brain MRI. CONCLUSION: Therapeutic drug monitoring of osimertinib and almonertinib in cerebrospinal fluid, rather than plasma alone, may provide a more relevant indicator for assessing and optimizing treatment efficacy against brain metastases in NSCLC. This study would develop personalized treatment plans for NSCLC patients with brain metastases, providing important evidence for clinical practice.

articles.title: Effects of St. John's Wort extract on the release of paracrine markers and neurite outgrowth in mouse hippocampal HT-22 neuronal cells co-cultured with SIM-A9 microglia.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hypericum perforatum L., commonly known as St. John's wort (SJW), has traditionally been used to treat nervous disorders, including depression. Exposure to chronic stress events can affect neuronal and microglial function and induce depression. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes are not entirely understood. Our investigation aimed to determine the effects of STW3-VI, a special SJW extract, on the paracrine signaling between microglia and neurons in vitro. METHODS: Co-cultures of mouse SIM-A9 microglia (SIM-A9) with mouse hippocampal HT-22 neuronal cells (HT-22) were treated with different concentrations of SJW, hyperoside, an active component of SJW. Escitalopram, or nerve growth factor (NGF) as a positive control. To further elucidate the paracrine signaling, cell viability, ELISA, neurite outgrowth, migration, and ProteomeProfile™ methods were applied. RESULTS: Incubation HT-22 with SJW, escitalopram, hyperoside, or NGF, co-cultured with SIM-A9, stimulated neurite formation compared to the negative control. Using as screening ProteomeProfiler™ and to validate ELISA analyses, in the presence of mouse SIM-A9, SJW at a concentration 0.50 μg/mL, as well as 0.019 μg/mL hyperoside or 2.10 μg/mL escitalopram, significantly increased the cholinergic differentiation factor (CDF/LIF) release compared to the respective control. After treatment of mouse hippocampal HT-22 with escitalopram, hyperoside, or NGF, the release of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 was increased. Interestingly, SJW and hyperoside inhibited the release of growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) in co-culture. All experiments were performed under unstimulated co-culture conditions. CONCLUSION: Our data show that, under unstimulated co-culture conditions without external stimulation, an increase in CDF/LIF levels in HT-22 cells in the presence of SIM-A9 cells, a reduction in GDF-15 release by SIM-A9 microglia, and stimulation of neurite growth may indicate a possible effect of SJW on paracrine release and neurite outgrowth. Furthermore, the results indicate that hyperoside, escitalopram, and NGF enhance IL-10 release. Since our findings were derived from in vitro experiments, we can only speculate that a similar effect might occur in patients with depressive disorders. Additional in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies are necessary to confirm this hypothesis.

articles.title: Impact of ARBs plus beta-blockers and other antihypertensives on cognitive impairment: a longitudinal study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for dementia, yet the specific neuroprotective benefits of different antihypertensive drug classes remain unclear. This longitudinal population-based cohort study evaluated the association between various antihypertensive agents, used as monotherapy or combination therapy, and the risk of cognitive impairment. METHODS: The present work is a retrospective cohort study based on electronic health records (EHR) provided by the Consellería de Sanitat Universal i Salut Pública (Valencian Regional Health Authority, Spain) from two different hospitals in Valencia: Arnau de Villanova and Hospital La Fe. The study included 28057 individuals aged ≥ 65  years receiving antihypertensive therapy. Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed to estimate time-to-event outcomes and hazard ratios for cognitive impairment. RESULTS: Loop diuretics and the combination of ARBs with beta-blockers, were associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment. Conversely, selective beta-blockers and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors were associated with an increased probability of impairment. CONCLUSION: Antihypertensive classes display divergent neuroprotective profiles. Loop diuretics, ARBs, and ARB-beta-blocker combinations appear protective, whereas ACE inhibitors and beta-blocker monotherapy show less favorable cognitive outcomes, highlighting the need for tailored pharmacological selection in aging populations.

articles.title: Potential drug-drug interaction risks of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors in outpatients: a retrospective analysis using two screening databases.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Potential drug-drug interactions (pDDIs) involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) pose significant risks in psychiatric care, where polypharmacy often exacerbates pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects through cytochrome P450 enzyme pathways. This retrospective study aimed to assess the prevalence, characteristics, and risk factors of pDDIs associated with SSRIs in outpatients. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study on outpatients admitted to Beijing Tongren Hospital from January 2023 to December 2024. The patients were ≧18 years old and treated with two or more drugs including at least one SSRI. Micromedex® and Lexi-Interact® were used to identify pDDIs and their severities, and logistic regression was employed to identify demographic predictors such as gender, age, and number of concomitant medications. RESULTS: A total of 3476 prescriptions involving 1186 patients were included in the analysis. A prevalence of 19.68% was observed, with an average of 2.05 pDDIs per affected prescription. 98.83% of interactions detected by Micromedex® were classified as major, whereas among those detected by Lexi-Interact®, 68.76% were classified as moderate and 21.50% as minor. Agreement between the two databases on severity was poor (Cohen's κ = 0.034) when the same drug pairs were rated by both. Common interacting drug classes included antipsychotics (292 instances), other antidepressants (207), blood glucose-lowering agents (207), antithrombotic agents (193), and calcium channel blockers (157). Predominant clinical consequences encompassed QT interval prolongation (569 cases), serotonin syndrome (390), bleeding (229), and hypoglycemia (207), aligning with serotonergic excess and platelet function theories. Female gender, middle age (40-64 years), and polypharmacy were significantly associated with higher pDDI risks. CONCLUSION: This retrospective study found pDDIs involving SSRIs relatively uncommon among general hospital outpatients, a broader, less-studied population than prior psychiatric or nursing home cohorts, yet still linked to severe outcomes, especially among female, middle-aged patients on polypharmacy. Discrepancies between interaction-severity databases underscored the need for multi-tool assessment. Future prospective, multi-centre studies are needed to inform safer outpatient psychiatric prescribing.

articles.title: Gender differences in depressive-like behavior in Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: A Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by both motor and non-motor symptoms, including depression, which markedly impairs patients' quality of life. Although sex differences have been described in PD progression, the mechanisms underlying gender-specific susceptibility to depressive symptoms remain poorly understood. METHODS: This study investigated sex-dependent differences in depressive-like behaviors and their underlying molecular mechanisms in an in vivo model of 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced dopaminergic degeneration, using adult male and female CD1 mice. RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that MPTP administration induced nigrostriatal degeneration and α-synuclein accumulation in both sexes, with more pronounced alterations in males. Male mice also exhibited greater depressive- and anxiety-like behaviors, accompanied by a marked reduction in 5-HT2C receptor expression, increased hippocampal acetylcholine levels, impaired expression of the synaptic markers PSD-95 and synaptophysin, and a stronger downregulation of the BDNF/PI3K/AKT pathway compared with females. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that sex significantly influences vulnerability to PD-associated depressive symptoms, with males showing greater behavioral and molecular impairment. Overall, our results highlight the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in PD research and support the development of personalized therapeutic strategies targeting non-motor symptoms.

articles.title: Intracerebroventricular delivery of an ODN peptide analog protects dopaminergic neurons and modulates miRNA expression in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by progressive dopaminergic neuron degeneration, accompanied by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and apoptosis. Octadecaneuropeptide, ODN, is an astroglia-derived neuropeptide known to exert potent antioxidant and anti-apoptotic effects, protecting neuronal cells against oxidative damage and inflammation both in vivo and in vitro. In the present study, we investigated the neuroprotective potential of OP, an iso-active ODN analog, in an acute MPTP-induced mouse model of PD. METHODS: Mice were assigned to four groups i.e., control, MPTP, OP, and MPTP plus OP. MPTP was administered intraperitoneally (3 × 20 mg/kg, 2-h intervals), followed 1 h later by an intracerebroventricular injection of the OP (10 ng/10 μL). Brains were collected on day 7 for real-time PCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and Biochemical analyses. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Intracerebroventricular administration of OP significantly prevented the loss of tyrosine hydroxylase expression and mediating neuroprotective effect with stimulation of antiapoptotic gene Bcl-2 in the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area in MPTP-treated mice. Moreover, OP markedly reduced MPTP-induced oxidative damage by reducing ROS overproduction and lipid peroxidation and enhancing antioxidant catalase activity. OP also stimulated ERK1/2 phosphorylation and reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes such as TNF-α and increased IL-10 mRNA levels. In addition, OP prevented MPTP-induced down regulation of tight junction proteins i.e. occludin, ZO-1 preserving blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity. Furthermore, OP abolished MPTP-induced dysregulation of PD-related microRNAs including miR-21-3p, miR-29a-5p and markedly increased miR-34b-5p expression in nigrostriatal DA neurons. Taken together, these findings indicate that OP exerts potent neuroprotective effects by reducing oxidative stress, preserving BBB integrity, and limiting neuroinflammation and apoptosis. OP may therefore represent a promising therapeutic candidate for preventing dopaminergic neurodegeneration through modulation of key molecular pathways, including microRNAs involved in oxidative neurodegeneration.

articles.title: Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles for co-delivery of paclitaxel and psoralen: a synergistic strategy to overcome multidrug resistance in triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.abstract: A series of magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles were synthesized through the chemical integration of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA), and lecithin, further functionalized with Pluronic F-127 (PEO-PPO-PEO). The ternary architecture afforded nanoparticles with well-defined spherical morphology, tunable particle sizes (69-166 nm), and high colloidal stability with zeta potentials exceeding -30 mV. Spectroscopic analyses, including FTIR, DSC, XRD and PLM, confirmed the successful incorporation of therapeutic agents within the ternary matrix, revealing their amorphous dispersion and strong intermolecular interactions with the carrier components. Magnetic characterization demonstrated retained superparamagnetic behavior, highlighting the magnetic responsiveness of the ternary system. In vitro studies against paclitaxel-resistant SUM159/TXR triple-negative breast cancer cells showed that the ternary nanoparticles enhanced cellular uptake, induced synergistic G0/G1 and G2/M cell cycle arrest, and promoted early-stage apoptosis. Co-encapsulation of psoralen and paclitaxel within the ternary hybrid framework amplified cytotoxic effects compared to individual formulations. In vivo evaluation using a xenograft tumor model confirmed superior tumor growth inhibition and minimal systemic toxicity. These results underscore the chemical design and structural optimization of Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles as a promising strategy to overcome multidrug resistance and enhance therapeutic efficacy in aggressive cancers. This study constructed an Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid delivery system co-loaded with superparamagnetic nanoparticles, PTX and PSO, achieving synergistic effects of magnetic targeting, hemotherapy and drug-resistance reversal, which provides a novel strategy for precise therapy of drug-resistant TNBC.

articles.title: A disproportionality analysis of adverse event reports for givinostat in the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS) database.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Givinostat was recently approved for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), but its real-world safety profile remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated givinostat-associated safety signals by data mining of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database. METHODS: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR), Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR), Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network (BCPNN), and Multi-item Gamma Poisson Shrinker (MGPS) were applied to 321 reports with givinostat as the primary suspect (PS) drug from Q1 2024 to Q1 2026. A likelihood ratio test (LRT) with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction further assessed whether specific adverse events (AEs) were disproportionately associated with serious outcomes. Serious versus non-serious cases were compared by logistic regression and univariate tests. RESULTS: At the system organ class (SOC) level, investigations (ROR 5.54), gastrointestinal disorders (ROR 4.09), and blood and lymphatic system disorders (ROR 3.43) showed the strongest signals. For the preferred term (PT) level, blood triglycerides exhibited the strongest signal (ROR 341.3), while platelet count decreased was the most frequently reported (n = 96, 29.9%). After BH adjustment, platelet count decreased was the only PT with a significantly lower serious proportion than the overall baseline (14.58% vs. 30.07%, adjusted p = 0.024). Time-to-Onset (TTO) Analysis showed that diarrhoea typically occurred within the first week, whereas platelet count decreased and thrombocytopenia had delayed median onset (15.5 days and 17 days, respectively). CONCLUSION: Our study identified thrombocytopenia and hypertriglyceridemia as the most prominent safety signals for givinostat, with platelet count decreased showing a statistically significant difference in serious proportion and a lower serious proportion than the overall baseline. These findings provide evidence-based targets for structured hematological and metabolic monitoring, particularly during the early treatment phase, to support risk management in DMD patients receiving givinostat.

articles.title: Glucocorticoid-centered drug spectrum of non-jaw osteonecrosis, a FAERS pharmacovigilance study with independent validation in Canada Vigilance and JADER.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To distinguish jaw misclassification and litigation-related reporting from non-jaw osteonecrosis signals and define their reproducible spectrum. METHODS: We analyzed 20,690,895 deduplicated Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports (2004Q1-2026Q2), using report-level adjudication and four disproportionality criteria. A descriptive jaw-propensity index (JPI) measured the share of each drug's osteonecrosis reports coded as "jaw." Reporter restrictions and comparisons with Canada Vigilance and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database examined reporting bias. These external databases recorded less solicitation. Additional analyses included glucocorticoid stratification, empirical null calibration with unmasking, indication restriction of every surviving non-glucocorticoid drug, time-to-onset modeling, and machine learning. Estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Of 47 signals, 27 passed jaw exclusion (JPI < 0.50) and reporter restriction; the final core was unchanged across thresholds of 0.30-0.70. Tenofovir disoproxil's reporting odds ratio (ROR) fell from 157.9 (153.4-162.6) to 6.33 (5.38-7.45) among health professionals; 84.5% of cases were lawyer-sourced. Canada Vigilance (6.24, 2.00-19.4) and JADER (10.5, 6.60-16.8) were consistent with a litigation-inflated FAERS estimate. Glucocorticoids were replicated in both databases (class RORs 10.3, 54.4). Drug JPI rankings were concordant (r = 0.985, 0.960). All 34 negative controls had ROR < 1 (median 0.16); unmasking rescaled other estimates approximately 2.35-fold. Within-indication analyses detected no residual excess for mycophenolate (0.89) or voxelotor (0.97). Asparaginase combined a within-leukemia residual signal (7.14, 5.10-10.0) with mechanistic evidence and JADER replication (75.7). CONCLUSION: The reproducible spectrum is glucocorticoid-centered, with the asparaginase class the best-supported residual and three drugs unresolved. Jaw misclassification, reporting context, and indication explain much of the apparent spectrum. Spontaneous reports cannot establish causation; these adjudications require cohort confirmation. The JPI and cross-jurisdiction comparisons may inform analyses of other misclassification-prone endpoints.

articles.title: Cyclosporin a directly binds CCL5: a novel mechanism in SJS/TEN revealed by network pharmacology.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis, the most acute and severe of severe cutaneous adverse reactions, has an annual incidence of 0.4-13 cases per million and mortality rates range from <10% in Stevens-Johnson syndrome to >40% in toxic epidermal necrolysis, with an overall mortality of approximately 20%. Cyclosporin A (CsA) is clinically effective in Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN), but its mechanism beyond calcineurin inhibition remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To identify novel therapeutic targets of CsA in SJS/TEN using network pharmacology and validate the most promising candidate experimentally. METHODS: Potential CsA targets were predicted using PharmMapper and SuperPred. SJS/TEN-associated genes were retrieved from GeneCards and OMIM. Common targets were analyzed via protein-protein interaction network, Gene Ontology, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment. Molecular docking predicted binding modes. The key target interaction was validated in vitro using MicroScale Thermophoresis. RESULTS: We identified 22 shared targets between CsA and SJS/TEN. Network analysis highlighted five core proteins (MMP9, CASP3, CCL5, CXCR4, CYP3A4). Molecular docking predicted stable binding between CsA and Chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 5 (CCL5). Critically, MST assays demonstrated direct physical interaction between CsA and CCL5 protein with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 2.7 μM. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our in vitro experiments confirmed a direct physical binding interaction between CsA and the key chemokine CCL5, providing a novel potential mechanistic hypothesis for the rapid anti-inflammatory effect of CsA in SJS/TEN. However, this hypothesis requires validation through cell-based chemotaxis assays.

articles.title: Natural compound ailanthone alleviates herpes simplex keratitis in mice by inhibiting HSV-1 replication.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Herpes simplex keratitis (HSK), caused by herpes simplex virus type I (HSV-1) infection, is a common ocular disease that can lead to corneal scarring and visual impairment. Since current antiviral drugs exhibit limited efficacy against HSK, it is necessary to explore new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of HSV-1 infection-related diseases. PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore the potential role of ailanthone, a plant-derived natural compound, as a therapeutic drug for reducing HSV-1 replication and alleviating the progression of HSK. METHODS: A library of natural compounds was screened and in vitro assays were performed to examine the inhibition of HSV-1 replication by ailanthone; Network pharmacology analysis and molecular docking prioritized integrin beta 2 (ITGB2) as a potential functional target of ailanthone. In vivo assays conducted to evaluate the anti-viral activity of ailanthone using an HSK mouse model. RESULTS: The study discovered that ailanthone is a potent HSV-1 inhibitor identified by screening. It suppressed viral gene expression and viral titers in vitro by downregulating ITGB2, a host factor supporting viral replication. Furthermore, ailanthone treatment at a low dose (1 mg/kg) and a high dose (5 mg/kg) significantly alleviated corneal lesions and reduced the corneal viral load in a mouse model of HSK. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, this study provided evidence that ITGB2 supported HSV-1 replication and identified a plant-derived natural compound, ailanthone, which suppresses HSV-1 replication via modulating ITGB2 expression, providing a potential drug candidate and therapeutic target for HSK treatment.

articles.title: The median effective dose of hyperbaric ropivacaine and lateral decubitus time for unilateral spinal anesthesia in lower extremity varicose vein surgery: a dose- and time-finding study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to determine the median effective dose (ED50) of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity and the median effective lateral decubitus time (ET50) for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity during lower extremity varicose vein surgery. METHODS: Sixty patients undergoing unilateral lower extremity varicose vein surgery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were enrolled in two sequential phases: a dose-finding phase (n = 30) and a time-finding phase (n = 30). All patients received intrathecal 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine. A modified Dixon up-and-down method was applied sequentially. In the dose-finding phase, the lateral decubitus position was maintained for 20 min. In the subsequent time-finding phase, patients received the ED5 of hyperbaric ropivacaine estimated in the dose-finding phase, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block in the non-surgical extremity. Successful prevention of motor block was defined as a modified Bromage score <1. For probit analysis, motor block (modified Bromage score ≥1) was coded as the positive response in the dose-finding phase, whereas successful prevention of motor block in the non-surgical extremity was coded as the positive response in the time-finding phase. The ED50 and ET50 were treated as the primary estimates, whereas additional quantile estimates derived from the fitted probit models were considered exploratory. RESULTS: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95% CI: 12.367-12.997 mg). The ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min). The exploratory ED5, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block, was 11.956 mg (95% CI, 10.304-12.303 mg), while the exploratory ET95 was 14.957 min (95% CI, 14.455-17.016 min). Adverse events were infrequent, and intraoperative hemodynamics remained stable. CONCLUSION: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95%CI: 12.367-12.997 mg), and the ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min). CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: [www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=239741], identifier [ChiCTR2400088340].

articles.title: Safety assessment of a Mitragyna speciosa leaf extract by a 90-day feeding study in rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitragyna speciosa is a deciduous evergreen tree belonging to the coffee (Rubiaceae) family. Traditionally used as a restorative, the extensive historical use data shows kratom has a low risk profile with respect to acute and chronic use. These conclusions cannot be unilaterally extended to all kratom products in the marketplace, of which there is a wide variety, with many far removed from traditional kratom preparations. METHODS: A 90-day toxicity study was conducted for the purpose of identifying a no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) for a proprietary extract prepared from M. speciosa leaf, standardized to a target mitragynine concentration. Sprague Dawley Crl:CD (SD) rats (80 male and 80 female) were grouped as 20 male and 20 female and dosed daily by gavage (10 mL/kg body weight) with SpecioTea™ supplying mitragynine at 0, 15, 30, or 60 mg/kg/day for 90 days. The following parameters and end points were evaluated in this study: clinical signs, body weights, body weight gains, food consumption, ophthalmology, clinical pathology parameters (hematology, coagulation, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis), gross necropsy findings, organ weights, and histopathologic examinations. RESULTS: Daily oral administration of SpecioTea™ resulted in dose-related reductions in food consumption and lower body weights at ≥15 mg/kg/day. Functional observation battery findings were generally consistent with the known pharmacology of the test article at ≥30 mg/kg/day and non-adverse clinical pathology findings at ≥15 mg/kg/day. Adverse changes were observed in the ovary, testis, and epididymis at 60 mg/kg/day. Thus 30 mg/kg b.w./day of SpecioTea™ was designated as NOAEL. CONCLUSION: Due to findings at all SpecioTea™ dose levels, a no-observed effect level (NOEL) could not be established. Based on the observed adverse changes in the ovary, testis, and epididymis at 60 mg/kg/day, the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) for SpecioTea™ is 30 mg/kg/day for males and females. The results from this study provides evidence in support of the low toxicity associated with a proprietary kratom leaf extract. Scientifically relevant data from studies such as this should form the basis through which further research on the benefits and safety of kratom products are conducted.

articles.title: Live combined bifidobacterium attenuates rivaroxaban-associated colonic bleeding in mice: evidence for a substantial gut microbiota-dependent component.
articles.abstract: Rivaroxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC), is widely prescribed for the prevention and treatment of thromboembolic disorders. However, its use is associated with an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding, the mechanisms of which remain incompletely understood. Effective strategies to relief such bleeding are also lacking. Because the gut microbiota plays a critical role in maintaining intestinal homeostasis, we investigated whether probiotics could mitigate anticoagulant-related bleeding and explored the underlying mechanisms. Using a rivaroxaban-induced mouse model of colonic bleeding, we found that treatment with live combined Bifidobacterium reduced occult blood in the feces, alleviated damage to colon tissue, and lowered serum levels of the inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α and chemokine ligand 5. Integrated 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomic analyses showed that LCB treatment was accompanied by alterations in the gut microbial community and fecal metabolic profile. Following antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, the overall ameliorative effect of LCB was attenuated, although partial responses, including a reduction in CXCL5, were retained. These findings support a substantial microbiota-dependent component of the full ameliorative phenotype. Untargeted metabolomic analysis identified a metabolite feature putatively annotated as anandamide that showed a nominal decrease following rivaroxaban administration and a nominal increase after LCB treatment. However, these differences did not remain significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction and were therefore considered exploratory. The same feature also showed a nominal increase following LCB treatment in antibiotic-treated mice without corresponding restoration of the overall ameliorative phenotype, suggesting that this metabolic change alone was insufficient to account for the observed effects. To our knowledge, the present study provides initial evidence that LCB administered after the onset of fecal occult bleeding ameliorates rivaroxaban-associated colonic injury in mice. Collectively, these findings suggest that the overall ameliorative effect of LCB has a substantial gut microbiota-dependent component, whereas the putative anandamide signal represents a hypothesis-generating metabolic association that requires targeted quantitative and functional validation.

articles.title: Successful application of low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation in CRRT for patients with liver failure: a retrospective case series study of 11 patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. METHOD: A retrospective case series study was conducted.
