Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. RESULTS: A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Predictive Toxicology and Drug Safety: From Preclinical Prediction to Post-Market Surveillance.
articles.abstract: Clinical development of drug candidates remains a significant problem in pharmaceutics. Approximately 90% of candidates entering clinical development fail to achieve regulatory approval across the full Phase I-III pathway, with unforeseen safety liabilities accounting for a substantial share of this attrition alongside efficacy, pharmacokinetic, and commercial factors. commonly cited estimates place development at 12-15 years and over USD 1 billion per approved drug, yet patients still suffer avoidable consequences. Predictive toxicology, the use of computational approaches to estimate toxicity risks, is essential in addressing this attrition, and recent AI and ML developments enable efficient analysis of complex datasets. This review evaluates AI-driven predictive toxicology against classical paradigms (QSAR, PBPK, rule-based expert systems), finding regulators favour established methods. AI augments rather than replaces validated frameworks. A decision-theoretic framework examines asymmetric consequences of false-positive and false-negative errors, including premature rejection of viable candidates, alongside data challenges (class imbalance, label uncertainty, dataset heterogeneity). Few case studies meet explicit criteria for AI-driven Drug Development and Safety Assessment informing a decision. Coverage spans the lifecycle, from preclinical prediction to post-market surveillance, including multi-omics, foundation models, and federated learning. AI adds value to drug safety, but requires prospective validation, methodology disclosure, and expert oversight.

articles.title: Case Report: Probable blinatumomab-associated lung injury in a pediatric patient with B-ALL.
articles.abstract: Blinatumomab is a bispecific T Cell engager targeting CD3 and CD19. Initially approved for relapsed/refractory B Cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), it was later extended to first-line B-ALL therapy. Despite its high efficacy, blinatumomab carries risks of adverse effects, including cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity. Blinatumomab-associated lung injury is exceptionally rare. We report a pediatric B-ALL patient who developed drug-induced lung injury following induction chemotherapy, with recurrence of lung injury after blinatumomab administration. The patient presented with dyspnea, hypoxemia, and radiographic findings suggestive of interstitial lung injury. After excluding infectious and other non-infectious etiologies, we considered blinatumomab-associated lung injury as the most likely diagnosis. Symptoms improved markedly following corticosteroid therapy. Clinicians should be alert to blinatumomab-associated lung injury, achieve early recognition and administer glucocorticoid intervention. A dose-escalation strategy facilitates successful rechallenge.

articles.title: N-Benzyl Indole-Benzoxazole Hybrids as Multi-Target Anticancer Agents Modulating mTOR, Apoptosis, and Lipid Dynamics in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Indole-benzoxazole hybrids are structurally versatile scaffolds with significant promise in anticancer drug development. This study aimed to synthesize N-benzyl-substituted indole-benzoxazole derivatives (IBB1-5) and to evaluate their antiproliferative potential and mechanistic effects in human breast cancer models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: IBB1-5 were synthesized and screened for cytotoxic activity against MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells using MTT assays. The most active compound, IBB-4, was further investigated in MDA-MB-231 cells through clonogenic assays and morphological analysis. Immunofluorescence staining was performed to assess mTOR, LC3, caspase-3, and β-tubulin expression and distribution. Lipid droplet dynamics were evaluated using Oil Red O and Nile Red staining, combined with three-dimensional surface-plot analysis. RESULTS: IBB-4 demonstrated the strongest growth-inhibitory activity, with IC50 values of 12.2 μM (MDA-MB-231) and 12.8 μM (MCF-7). Clonogenic assays revealed significant dose-dependent suppression of long-term proliferative capacity. Morphological alterations included cytoplasmic vacuolization and structural disorganization. Immunofluorescence analyses showed a marked downregulation of mTOR and a spatial redistribution of LC3, without significant changes in total fluorescence intensity. Increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity and pronounced disruption of β-tubulin indicated activation of apoptotic pathways and cytoskeletal destabilization. Lipid staining, supported by three-dimensional surface analysis, demonstrated prominent clustering and redistribution of intracellular lipid droplets. CONCLUSION: IBB-4 exerts multi-layered anticancer effects through coordinated modulation of proliferative signaling, apoptotic activation, cytoskeletal integrity, and lipid compartmentalization. These findings identify IBB-4 as a promising lead candidate for further molecular and preclinical investigations, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer.

articles.title: Assessment of Allometric Scaling Methods for the Prediction of Human Pharmacokinetic of LNA-i-miR-221.
articles.abstract: Antisense oligonucleotides are small synthetic DNA or RNA molecules that can be used to modulate gene expression, particularly to block the production of unwanted proteins. This makes them potentially powerful drugs to contrast cancer growth. Drug development is a long process that includes preclinical and clinical studies. Preclinical animal studies are designed to assess drug kinetics and safety before progressing to clinical trials, as they may predict the therapeutic dose to be used in the "first in human" (FIH) studies. This is usually achieved by applying allometric scaling methods that allow predicting the human pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters from those estimated in animals. Selecting the appropriate scaling formula reduces the risk of translational uncertainty and supports the design of FIH studies. The aim of this study is to compare the accuracy of different allometric scaling methods in predicting human PK of the antisense oligonucleotide LNA-i-miR-221, a powerful inhibitor of microRNA miR-221, which was found to be deregulated in several malignancies, favoring cancer progression. To do that, we exploited the availability of PK data of the drug in both Sprague Dawley rats and humans and we found that the best scaling method for both clearance and distribution volume is the simple allometry, with predictions laying within the 2-fold and 4-fold error interval, respectively. This study contributes to identifying the most accurate scaling methods among the evaluated single-species approaches to extrapolate human pharmacokinetic for LNA-i-miR-221, possibly offering a starting point for future studies involving antisense oligonucleotides.

articles.title: Safety profile of desmopressin and risk signals for hyponatremia: evidence from FAERS and CVARDD real-world databases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Desmopressin has been associated with hyponatremia-in clinical practice; however, postmarketing real-world evidence on its safety signals, susceptible populations, and time-to-onset (TTO) patterns remains limited. METHODS: This study aimed to characterize desmopressin related adverse event signals in the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS,2004Q1-2025Q4) and the Canadian Vigilance Adverse Reaction Database (CVARDD), focusing on hyponatremia. Signal detection was performed using four disproportionality analysis methods (reporting odds ratio, proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker), with concurrent positivity across all four methods required for signal confirmation. Subgroup analyses were conducted by age and sex. For cases with complete dates, TTO was calculated and modeled using the Weibull distribution. RESULTS: Among 19,906,480 deduplicated reports, 3,878 listed desmopressin as the primary suspect drug. The strongest signals were observed for metabolism and nutrition disorders, particularly hyponatremia-related events (e.g., Hyponatraemia, Blood sodium decreased, Water intoxication, Hyponatraemic encephalopathy), often accompanied by seizures and other serious neurologic events. Age was the main source of heterogeneity: hyponatremia-related RORs were markedly higher in patients aged ≥ 60 years. TTO analysis showed an early-failure pattern, with ~ 60% of AEs occurring within 30 days; the Weibull shape parameter β = 0.36 (95% CI 0.35-0.37) indicated a decreasing hazard over time. Hyponatremia also occurred predominantly early but remained detectable during long-term treatment (≥ 360 days). CONCLUSION: Hyponatremia-related events represented prominent reporting signals for desmopressin in spontaneous-report databases. Cross-database assessment, subgroup heterogeneity, and TTO patterns provide pharmacovigilance context for this established safety concern. These findings characterize reporting patterns and do not quantify clinical incidence or establish causality. They support continued adherence to existing recommendations for patient selection and sodium monitoring during desmopressin therapy.

articles.title: Citrus lemon-derived nanovesicles induced collagen expression in UVB-induced photoaged models.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Various vesicle-based therapeutic strategies have recently been investigated as potential approaches for skin rejuvenation and anti-aging. In this study, the rejuvenating effects of Citrus lemon-derived nanovesicles (CLDNVs) on photoaged skin were evaluated in a murine model. METHODS: CLDNVs were isolated and characterized based on their morphology, concentration, particle size, and surface markers. The cytotoxicity of CLDNVs on human dermal fibroblast cells was assessed using the MTT assay. Female C57BL/6 mice were exposed to UVB radiation for 10 weeks to induce photoaging. Subsequently, they were treated for 28 days with CLDNVs (300 µg/mL) either alone or in combination with 0.05% retinoic acid. The anti-aging effects of the treatments were evaluated on days 14 and 28 using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, Masson's Trichrome staining, and immunofluorescence analysis of Col1a1 protein expression. The relative mRNA expression of type I collagen and matrix metalloproteinases (Mmp1 and Mmp3) were determined by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). RESULTS: Treatment with CLDNVs significantly reduced epidermal thickness compared with the UVB-irradiated group (P < 0.0001). The Collagen-positive area was significantly increased in both the CLDNV-treated and retinoic acid-treated groups compared with the UVB-irradiated group (P < 0.0001). Furthermore, IF analysis demonstrated a significant increase in collagen levels in the CLDNV-treated group compared with the UVB-irradiated group (p < 0.001). Moreover, CLDNV treatment significantly upregulated Col1a1 expression (P < 0.0001) and downregulated Mmp1 expression compared with the UVB-irradiated group. CONCLUSION: CLDNVs demonstrated promising potential as a natural and effective approach for mitigating UVB-induced skin photoaging. Their beneficial effects were associated with reduced epidermal thickness and enhanced type I collagen production, as evidenced by increased Cola1 gene and protein expression. These findings suggest that CLDNVs may represent a promising candidate for the development of novel strategies for the prevention or treatment of photoaging.

articles.title: Preparation of Honey-Loaded Liposomes and Evaluation of Their Physicochemical and Antibacterial Properties.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Honey is a natural wound-healing agent with antibacterial properties. It is applied to wounds in pure form or in conventional formulations; however, its application and efficacy may be challenging. Liposomes have been used as promising carriers for natural products. Therefore, honey-loaded liposomes were prepared and investigated as novel carriers for honey. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to prepare honey-loaded liposomes using different honey concentrations and to characterize the formulations. METHODS: Honey-loaded liposomes were prepared using the thin-film hydration method with egg lecithin and cholesterol at an 8:2 molar ratio and were hydrated with aqueous solutions containing 5% - 75% (w/v) honey. The mean particle size and zeta potential were measured by dynamic light scattering. Surface morphology was characterized by electron microscopy. Entrapment efficiency and the percentage of honey released were evaluated by quantifying honey polyphenols using the Folin-Ciocalteu assay as a marker of honey content. The minimum inhibitory concentration and minimum bactericidal concentration against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa were determined using a microdilution method. RESULTS: The liposomes had particle sizes of 94 - 282 nm, with the highest initial honey concentration (75%) yielding the largest particle size. Entrapment efficiencies were 22%-46%, with the 50% initial honey concentration showing the highest value. Increasing the initial honey concentration increased the honey content in the formulations. The zeta potential of plain liposomes was approximately -16 mV and shifted toward neutral values in honey-loaded liposomes (approximately -8 to -4 mV). Honey-loaded liposomes appeared as spherical particles, with some distorted spherical/angular particles. Honey release from liposomes showed a more extended pattern than that of honey solutions and followed Fickian diffusion kinetics from spheres for liposomes prepared with 5%-50% honey concentrations, whereas liposomes with a 75% initial honey concentration apparently favored first-order release kinetics. Biological assays showed enhanced antibacterial effects of liposomes of up to 3.5-fold and 7-fold against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, respectively, compared with honey. The liposomal formulation with 75% initial honey showed the highest antibacterial activity. CONCLUSIONS: The present results demonstrate that liposomes can deliver honey compounds and that honey-loaded liposomes may be promising candidates for medical applications, such as wound treatment.

articles.title: Editorial: Mechanisms of drug resistance in cancer: overcoming barriers with novel pharmacological strategies.
Linezolid-loaded Semi-solid Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations for Topical Wound Management: Preparation, In Vitro and Ex Vivo Characterization, Antimicrobial Activity and Radiolabeling Evaluation.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The present study aimed to develop and comprehensively characterize Linezolid (LZD)-loaded Semi-Solid Lipid Nanoparticles (SSLNs) as a potential topical delivery system for wound management. METHODS: We prepared SSLN formulations by high-shear homogenization. We characterized the formulations by physicochemical properties, encapsulation efficiency, mechanical and rheological behavior, in vitro release, ex vivo skin diffusion, radiolabeling efficiency, cellular association, and antimicrobial activity. RESULTS: The selected formulation (F11) exhibited a particle size of 437.2 ± 38.7 nm, PDI of 0.425 ± 0.069, zeta potential of -21.8 ± 0.7 mV, encapsulation efficiency of 81.3 ± 2.7%, and a pH of 5.81, together with shear-thinning rheological behavior. In vitro release studies demonstrated sustained drug release compared to the LZD solution. Ex vivo diffusion studies showed gradual, time-dependent permeation, reaching 839.28 μg/cm² at 24 h (68.7% of the applied dose). Radiolabeling with 99ᵐTc achieved an apparent radiolabeling efficiency above 90% under the employed RTLC conditions, and the chromatographic labeling profile was maintained over 6 h. In HaCaT cells, 99ᵐTc-labeled LZD-SSLNs showed significantly higher cell-associated radioactivity (83.80 ± 6.43%-88.41 ± 0.85%) than blank SSLNs (68.81 ± 5.04%-69.37 ± 7.37%). The F11 formulation exhibited antibacterial activity against the tested Gram-positive strains, with inhibition zones of 33 mm (S. aureus), 30 mm (E. faecalis), and 45 mm (B. subtilis), while the blank formulation showed no inhibition. DISCUSSION: The obtained findings indicate that the developed SSLN system provides sustained LZD release and a gradual, time-dependent skin permeation profile while exhibiting greater cell-associated radioactivity than the blank formulation and demonstrating antibacterial activity. Together, the sustained-release and timedependent permeation profiles, the greater cell-associated radioactivity observed for the LZD-loaded formulation, and antibacterial activity support further investigation of the SSLN system for topical delivery applications. CONCLUSION: Overall, LZD-loaded SSLNs demonstrated sustained release, time-dependent skin permeation, an apparent 99ᵐTc radiolabeling efficiency above 90% under the employed RTLC conditions, greater cellassociated radioactivity than the blank formulation, and antibacterial activity against the tested Gram-positive strains, supporting further investigation of this system for topical wound management.

articles.title: Antioxidant response and neurotransmitter modulation driven by oleuropein/alpha-lipoic acid attenuates lead-induced reproductive toxicity and neurotoxicity in Drosophila melanogaster.
articles.abstract: Lead is a ubiquitous environmental and industrial toxicant known to cause reproductive toxicity and neurotoxicity via the induction of oxidative damage and modulation of neurotransmitters. On the other hand, oleuropein and alpha-lipoic acid have independently been reported to demonstrate antioxidant and neurotransmitter modulatory activities. Here, we evaluated the protective role of oleuropein/alpha lipoic acid in lead-induced reproductive toxicity and neurotoxicity in Drosophila melanogaster. A 7-day survival analysis was carried out, and subsequently, flies were exposed to vehicle, lead acetate (20 mg/kg diet), and/or oleuropein and alpha lipoic acid (0.1 mg/kg diet) for 7 days. Oleuropein and alpha lipoic acid restored lead-induced weight loss and suppression of reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and catalase activities, as well as elevated malondialdehyde contents. In addition, oleuropein and alpha lipoic acid ameliorated lead-induced increases in acetylcholinesterase and monoamine oxidase activities and reductions in acetylcholine, dopamine, and serotonin in flies. Additionally, lead-induced disruption of climbing activity, courtship and mating latencies, mating duration, copulation success rate, and emergence rate were ameliorated by oleuropein and alpha lipoic acid in D. melanogaster. Overall, oleuropein and alpha lipoic acid attenuated lead-induced reproductive toxicity and neurotoxicity in D. melanogaster. Thus, oleuropein/alpha lipoic acid is a promising candidate for further investigation against lead-induced toxicity.

articles.title: Current Use and Practice of Opioids and Opiophobia in Modern Medicine: A Structured Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Opioids remain indispensable analgesics for acute, cancer-related, and selected chronic pain, yet their use is increasingly constrained by the opioid crisis and by opiophobia, an excessive, often irrational fear of opioid prescribing and use. This review synthesises evidence on opioid pharmacology, clinical applications, adverse effects, and opiophobia. METHODS: This structured narrative review followed the SANRA criteria; PRISMA and PRISMA-ScR frameworks were not applied. Five databases (Google Scholar, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE; 2010-2026) were searched, prioritising systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomised trials, and guidelines. Sixty-nine sources were synthesised. RESULTS: Opioids act mainly via μ-opioid receptors, suppressing ascending nociceptive transmission and enhancing descending inhibition. Agents differ in potency, onset, duration, metabolism, and adverse-effect profiles. Constipation, nausea, and sedation are common; respiratory depression, although uncommon at titrated doses, is the most serious hazard. Opiophobic attitudes were reported in up to 80.2% of emergency physicians, and up to 64.4% of cancer patients held extreme addiction concerns. The pooled prevalence of opioid use disorder or dependence during long-term opioid therapy for chronic non-cancer pain was 9.3% (95% CI 5.7-14.8%). DISCUSSION: Attitudinal barriers, rather than pharmacological limitations alone, drive undertreatment of pain, and regulatory overcorrection after the opioid crisis has created a secondary burden of inadequate analgesia. Risk stratification, multimodal analgesia, and structured monitoring can limit opioid exposure while preserving effective analgesia. CONCLUSION: Opioids remain effective and manageable under appropriate supervision. Balanced, evidence-based prescribing frameworks, combined with prescriber and patient education, are essential to reduce harm from both opioid misuse and inadequate analgesia.

articles.title: 2D-QSAR and Molecular Docking Studies of 5-Nitrofuranyl Derivatives as Potential Galactofuranosyltransferase 2 Inhibitors for Antitubercular Therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) is a transmissible disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which continues to be a major public health issue worldwide. The situation has become more alarming with the increasing cases of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains, which makes treatment difficult. Nitrofurans, a class of heterocyclic compounds known for their antimicrobial potential, have gained renewed attention as scaffolds for anti-TB drug design. This study aimed to investigate the structural features governing the antitubercular activity of 5-nitrofuranyl derivatives using 2D-QSAR modeling and molecular docking analysis and to identify new compounds that inhibit the biosynthesis of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall. METHOD: Twenty-eight 5-nitrofuranyl derivatives were studied by means of 2D-QSAR analysis employing descriptors from the Dragon software suite within the framework of CP-MLR methodology. Statistically significant models were selected based on r², Q² (LOO and L5O), and test set predictivity. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock Vina against Galactofuranosyltransferase 2 (GlfT2), a validated target involved in the cell wall biosynthesis of M. tuberculosis. RESULT: Robust QSAR models were obtained with up to R² = 0.912 and Q²LOO = 0.839. Key descriptors influencing activity included topological descriptors (IC1, JGI2, JGI5), mass-weighted Burden eigenvalues (BELm2, BELm6), molecular weight (MW), and selected atom-centered fragments such as C-006 and C-031. Docking studies revealed that several compounds (notably 27, 25, and 3) exhibited high binding affinity to GlfT2 (-9 to -6.7 kcal/mol), correlating well with QSAR predictions. DISCUSSION: The obtained QSAR parameters suggested the importance of molecular topology, electronic features, and particular structural fragments in modulating antitubercular activity. Molecular docking to the GlfT2 protein showed that the binding affinity of compounds 27, 25, and 3 was found to be more favorable for their binding in the active site of the enzyme. Moreover, the results from the ADME study demonstrated that compound 3 acquired the best pharmacokinetic properties compared to the other molecules. CONCLUSION: This integrated QSAR and molecular modeling study highlights the structural determinants of 5- nitrofuranyl-based antituberculosis agents. Compounds with favorable descriptor profiles and strong GlfT2 binding affinity represent promising leads for further development. This approach demonstrates the effectiveness of combining ligand- and structure-based strategies for rational antitubercular drug design.

articles.title: Nanotherapeutic Strategies for Overcoming Cancer Drug Resistance: A Review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Cancer comprises heterogeneous diseases driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations that enable uncontrolled proliferation, survival, and metastasis. Drug resistance remains a principal cause of treatment failure and recurrence. This review evaluates nanotherapeutic strategies designed to overcome resistance mechanisms and improve therapeutic outcomes in oncology. METHODS: We conducted a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature and clinical data on resistance pathways and nanocarrier platforms. Mechanisms examined include transporter-mediated efflux (P-gp, BCRP, MRP1), enhanced DNA repair, apoptosis evasion, epigenetic reprogramming, and cancer stem cell persistence. Advances in spatial and single-cell profiling informing tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental influences were integrated. Nanocarrier systems assessed include liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, and stimuli-responsive platforms. RESULTS: Over two decades, nanomedicines such as Doxi and Onivyde have demonstrated clinical utility in surmounting biological barriers to drug delivery. Targeted nanotherapies enable passive and active targeting, controlled release, and rational combination regimens that mitigate multidrug resistance and enhance selective cytotoxicity. Emerging AI-guided design, tumor microenvironment remodeling, STING pathway activation, and immunogenic cell death induction are accelerating next-generation nano-immunotherapeutics. DISCUSSION: These findings indicate that rational nanocarrier engineering, informed by high-resolution tumor biology, can meaningfully improve drug bioavailability, targeting specificity, and therapeutic index. However, variability in tumor biology, incomplete understanding of nano-bio interactions, and challenges in biomarker discovery, manufacturing scale-up, and regulatory pathways constrain translation. CONCLUSION: Nanotherapy holds substantial promise for overcoming cancer drug resistance, yet realizing its potential requires interdisciplinary collaboration, mechanism-driven design, and rigorous clinical validation to ensure scalable, biomarker-guided, and regulatory-compliant applications.

articles.title: Integrated Computational Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Identify the PLK2-TFEB Axis as a Therapeutic Mechanism of Kunkui Baoshen Decoction in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Metabolic stress and lipid homeostasis imbalance in proximal tubular cells (PTC) are increasingly recognized as critical contributors to diabetic kidney disease (DKD) progression, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Kunkui Baoshen Decoction (KKBS) has shown clinical benefits in DKD, but its molecular basis remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the therapeutic targets and regulatory mechanisms of KKBS in DKD-associated proximal tubular injury. METHODS: An integrated multi-omics strategy combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, machine learning, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was applied to identify candidate therapeutic targets of KKBS in DKD. Then, the protective effects of KKBS were further evaluated in db/db mice and high-glucose and high-lipid (HGHL)-induced HK-2 cells by assessing renal function, lipid metabolism, autophagic flux, transcription factor EB (TFEB) nuclear translocation, and fibrosis-related markers. RESULTS: KKBS effectively reduced urinary protein excretion, corrected aberrant lipid metabolism, and mitigated renal fibrotic lesions in db/db mice. Integrated multi-omics profiling highlighted polo-like kinase 2 (PLK2) as a potential therapeutic target, and scRNA-seq analysis demonstrated its progressive upregulation in PTC during DKD progression. Mechanistically, KKBS treatment reduced PLK2 expression, restored TFEB nuclear translocation, improved autophagic flux, and decreased lipid droplet accumulation. Similar effects were reproduced by PLK2 inhibition in HGHL-induced HK-2 cells. DISCUSSION: These findings support the PLK2-TFEB axis as a potential therapeutic target in DKD. CONCLUSION: KKBS may alleviate lipid accumulation and fibrotic alterations in DKD by suppressing PLK2 expression, facilitating TFEB nuclear translocation, and restoring autophagy-lysosome-related function.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety profile of advanced therapies in Crohn's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disorder characterized by a relapsing-remitting course and substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation. This study aimed to assess the comparative efficacy and safety of approved biologic and small-molecule therapies for CD, with particular emphasis on guselkumab and mirikizumab. METHODS: A systematic review and frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-NMA, the Cochrane Handbook, and ISPOR guidelines. MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2026. Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating adalimumab, guselkumab, infliximab, mirikizumab, risankizumab, vedolizumab, upadacitinib, or ustekinumab in adults with CD were included. RESULTS: A total of 27 RCTs were included. During induction therapy, guselkumab 400 mg achieved the highest P-scores for both clinical response and remission and was associated with higher odds of these outcomes compared with placebo and several active comparators. Mirikizumab was also more effective than placebo but ranked in the middle of the treatment hierarchy. During maintenance therapy, guselkumab 200 mg and 100 mg achieved the highest rankings for clinical response and remission; however, differences between guselkumab and several active comparators were not statistically significant. These comparisons were predominantly informed by indirect evidence and should not be interpreted as establishing definitive clinical superiority. No consistent evidence of major safety differences was observed across interventions; however, heterogeneity and inconsistency in several safety networks limited the certainty of the comparisons. Although guselkumab achieved favourable rankings for serious adverse events and serious infections, few statistically significant differences were observed between active treatments. The results should be interpreted in the context of indirect comparisons and methodological heterogeneity among included studies. CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of an NMA based predominantly on indirect evidence, guselkumab achieved the highest rankings for several efficacy outcomes during both induction and maintenance therapy. Mirikizumab showed higher odds of response and remission than placebo, although its node was informed by a single eligible phase 3 study. Given differences in study populations and trial designs, particularly in maintenance studies, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and not as evidence of definitive clinical superiority.

articles.title: Adolescent fluoxetine exposure as a developmental cause of anxiety-like behavior in adult female mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) fluoxetine (FLX) is a first-line pharmacological treatment for mood-related illnesses in the adolescent population - in which girls exhibit approximately twice the risk of being diagnosed with such disorders. Despite increasing FLX prescription rates in adolescents, the potential for unexpected long-term side effects remains poorly understood. To address this issue, we evaluated whether juvenile FLX exposure alters baseline responses to anxiety-inducing environments in adulthood. METHODS: Adolescent female C57BL/6 mice received FLX (20 mg/kg) for 15 consecutive days (postnatal day [PD] 35-49). Three weeks later, once the mice reached adulthood (PD70), separate groups of mice were evaluated on the novelty suppressed feeding test or the elevated plus maze, two behavioral tasks validated for the assessment of anxiety-related responses. RESULTS: We found that adult female mice with adolescent FLX pre-exposure displayed decreases in body weight and exploratory behavior in the elevated plus maze, along with a longer latency to initiate feeding behavior in the novelty suppressed feeding test, without changes in locomotor activity. CONCLUSION: Our data show that adolescent exposure to FLX results in anxiety-like phenotypes in adulthood, suggesting that early-life SSRI exposure may induce long-term changes in neural circuits regulating affective-related behavior.

articles.title: Identification of highly specific bacterial L-asparaginase through genome-wide computational screening and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bacterial L-asparaginases are key therapeutics for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but their clinical efficacy is limited by off-target L-glutaminase co-activity, which contributes to severe side effects. This study aimed to identify highly specific bacterial L-asparaginases with minimal L-glutaminase co-activity. METHODS: We screened ~ 85,000 prokaryotic genomes using a workflow integrating AlphaFold2 structure prediction, molecular docking, binding-energy estimation, and molecular dynamics simulations. Six top-ranked enzymes were selected for experimental validation. RESULTS: RhAII protein from Acidobacteriota sp. showed high specificity toward L-asparagine (L-Asn), with a Michaelis constant (KM) of 12 ± 2 µM and turnover number (kcat) of 34 ± 2 s⁻¹, and negligible L-glutaminase activity. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a relationship between enzyme activity and the conformational dynamics of the flexible gating element (FGE), characterized by residue-level root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), and L-Asn positional fluctuations, evaluated by ligand root mean square deviation (RMSD) relative to the protein. High L-asparaginase activity was associated with optimal FGE dynamics and low L-Asn RMSD, consistent with stable substrate positioning within the active site. In contrast, enzymes with altered FGE dynamics relative to the reference EcAII enzyme from Escherichia coli, such as PoAII from Planctomycetota sp., showed poor L-asparaginase performance (KM 5797 ± 1143 µM; kcat 1.2 ± 0.1 s⁻¹). CONCLUSIONS: Genome- and structure-guided screening identified RhAII as a promising antileukemic candidate for further validation in biological models. A key limitation of the computational workflow was the lack of correlation between predicted substrate binding energies and catalytic efficiency, highlighting the importance of active-site dynamics in enzyme kinetics.

articles.title: The positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062, attenuates alcohol self-administration in female Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Four-day intragastric treatment with the positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062 (1, 3, and 10 mg/kg), suppressed operant oral alcohol self-administration in male and female Sprague Dawley (SD) rats (Haile et al., Psychopharmacology 238:2587-2600, 2021). Conversely, in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 6-week treatment with ASP8062 (25 mg/day, corresponding to the 3-mg/kg rat dose) failed to attenuate alcohol craving and consumption in individuals with moderate or severe alcohol use disorder (AUD) (Schacht et al., Alcohol Clin Exp Res 48:2352-2363, 2024). Reverse-translational dose-ranging studies in animal models of AUD were suggested. OBJECTIVES: In keeping with this purpose, the present study tested ASP8062 on operant oral alcohol self-administration in selectively bred Sardinian alcohol-preferring (sP) rats, a validated animal model of AUD. METHODS: Female sP rats were trained to lever-respond for alcohol under the fixed ratio 5 schedule of reinforcement. Once lever-responding for alcohol was high and steady, rats underwent a 4-day intragastric treatment with ASP8062 (3, 10, and 17 mg/kg). RESULTS: Only the 17-mg/kg dose reduced, by approximately 40%, lever-responding for alcohol and estimated amount of self-administered alcohol. No dose of ASP8062 altered motor-coordination, as indicated by the results of a concurrent inverted-screen test. CONCLUSIONS: ASP8062 in sP rats was remarkably less potent compared to previous observations in SD rats, suggesting that higher doses of ASP8062 may be needed in rats modeling AUD. If ideally transposed to humans, these data suggest that future clinical studies should consider testing higher doses of ASP8062 before reaching definitive conclusions on its therapeutic potential.
